title: Binance Hackers Deploy ‘Never-Seen-Before’ Crypto Laundering Tactics
summary: Chainalysis identified previously unseen laundering patterns as attackers circulated stolen Binance assets through thousands of transactions, suggesting automated efforts to obscure the trail. Its investigation also linked the theft to North Korean hackers. Thousands of Transfers Point to Automated ...
content:
Chainalysis identified previously unseen laundering patterns as attackers circulated stolen Binance assets through thousands of transactions, suggesting automated efforts to obscure the trail. Its investigation also linked the theft to North Korean hackers.

Key Takeaways

  • Recurring wallet activity suggests automated laundering of stolen assets.
  • Stolen Binance assets mixed with funds from September’s Bitget theft.
  • Attackers exchanged $325 million in stablecoins for $285 million in ether.

Thousands of Transfers Point to Automated Laundering

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis identified suspected automated laundering on Oct. 30 after a Binance theft it estimated at $6.4 billion, which it called the largest crypto theft on record. The company stated:

“Our investigators are observing never-seen-before laundering patterns with the stolen funds from the Binance exploit.”

Thousands of transactions in a short period suggested automation intended to obscure the trail.

Investigators tracked repeated transfers among addresses, including returns to wallets used earlier in the sequence. Many addresses first received exactly 1 TRX, Tron’s native token used to pay transaction fees, before accepting more funds and forwarding assets elsewhere. Chainalysis added: “This repeated sequence suggests a programmatic process for moving and redistributing the stolen funds.”

Investigators Trace Access and a North Korea Connection

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng disclosed additional breach points and bypassed approval controls, alongside a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tools and traces. Chainalysis traced outflows to about 4:20 p.m. Eastern time on Oct. 29 and identified an Ethereum wallet funded through Tornado Cash, a crypto mixer that obscures links between deposits and withdrawals. That wallet submitted valid signed authorizations, or cryptographically signed permissions, enabling a Binance hot wallet to run attacker-deployed software and transfer assets into attacker-controlled addresses.

Laundering patterns initially suggested involvement by Tradertraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group. Chainalysis then observed stolen Binance assets mixing with proceeds from September’s Bitget theft, previously attributed to North Korean actors, strengthening its attribution of the hack to Tradertraitor. Separately, TRM Labs attributed the Binance attack to Tradertraitor with high confidence, citing onchain and offchain intelligence.

Stablecoin Swaps Race Against Asset Freezes

Chainalysis explained:

“Freezing funds takes time. The attacker attempted to stay ahead of that process by quickly moving $500 million of stablecoins into a wallet whose job it was to swap out those freezable assets to non-freezable assets.”

Such stablecoin freeze and blacklist controls can prevent designated addresses from transferring affected tokens, while native ether has no equivalent issuer-controlled mechanism.

Over nearly 20 minutes, the wallet exchanged $325 million in stablecoins for approximately $285 million in ether, then moved the remaining $175 million to intermediary wallets 10 minutes later. Freezes began by 5:14 p.m. Eastern time on Oct. 29, with Chainalysis reporting about $2.8 billion frozen in its Oct. 30 account. Binance separately put the total at approximately $3 billion that day.

The exchange also said it had reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the incident, excluding frozen assets. Of that amount, $5 billion was already held in affected tokens. Purchases through market and over-the-counter channels were underway to match the remaining assets.

title: Binance Prepares to Resume Withdrawals, Unveils $6.3B Hack Recovery Plan
summary: Binance is preparing to restore withdrawals in phases after its $6.3 billion hack, with reopening dependent on security checks. The exchange committed company funds to replace stolen assets while investigators expanded their review of the breach. Withdrawals Face Security Checks Before Phased Restar...
content:
Binance is preparing to restore withdrawals in phases after its $6.3 billion hack, with reopening dependent on security checks. The exchange committed company funds to replace stolen assets while investigators expanded their review of the breach.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance targeted a phased withdrawal restart, subject to completed security checks.
  • Matching tokens worth $5 billion cover approximately 80% of losses.
  • Binance said partners froze about $3 billion in stolen assets.

Withdrawals Face Security Checks Before Phased Restart

Binance outlined a four-part hack recovery plan on Oct. 30 in its second Security Incident Update, targeting the start of withdrawal restoration within approximately 34 hours of the update. Its phased withdrawal restart remained subject to completed security checks, remediation, and validation of affected systems. Deposits and other unaffected services remained operational, according to the announcement.

Co-CEOs Yi He and Richard Teng signed the update, which placed the hot-wallet compromise at approximately 8:05 p.m. UTC on Oct. 29. Addressing the estimated $6.3 billion loss, the statement emphasized:

“Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.”

The exchange pledged coverage through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate treasury, or company financial reserves.

Token Purchases and Asset Freezes Anchor Recovery

More than $6.34 billion in company funds reserved for losses included $5 billion already held in the affected token assets, Binance said. Those holdings matched approximately 80% of losses involving assets such as USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH, and BNB. Purchases through market and over-the-counter channels were underway to obtain the remaining matching tokens.

Approximately $3 billion had been frozen onchain, Binance reported, while recovery efforts continued with law enforcement, token issuers, intelligence firms, and other exchanges. Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic’s independent analysis of tracing and freezing stolen assets put verified freezes at $2.84 billion as of its 8 a.m. UTC update on Oct. 30, predominantly involving USDT and USDC. Frozen funds remained subject to recovery efforts.

Investigators tracing stolen assets can examine wallet balances and transfers through public blockchain transaction records. Separately, Binance planned an initial proof-of-reserves snapshot within 12 hours of its announcement. Results were expected by Monday, Nov. 2, showing platform holdings against customer balances.

Expanded Investigation Examines Signing Access

The initial laptop-compromise findings suggested a compromised DevOps engineer’s computer enabled unauthorized withdrawal submissions. DevOps engineers maintain software deployment and the infrastructure supporting it. Binance maintained that it had found no evidence of leaked wallet private keys.

Teng’s separate Oct. 30 video described additional breach points, bypassed approval controls, and a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tools and traces. Binance said it had contained compromised infrastructure, revoked affected authorizations, and introduced further controls against unauthorized activity. Internal and external specialists were working to reconstruct the full attack sequence.

Blockchain security firm Hypernative’s analysis identified compromised signing access and valid signatures from Binance-controlled keys. It described the use of EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets a regular wallet execute smart-contract code, to run attacker-controlled code through a Binance wallet. Binance expected further verified technical findings within about 48 hours of its announcement, subject to investigative considerations, followed by a detailed post-mortem covering the attack and safeguards.

title: Senators Warren, Curtis Press Kalshi and Polymarket on Election Insider Trading
summary: Sens. Elizabeth Warren and John Curtis have asked Kalshi and Polymarket to explain how they keep insiders out of election markets, giving the companies until Nov. 3, Election Day, to answer seven questions. The bipartisan letter cites candidates who bet on their own races and suspected wash trading ...
content:
Sens. Elizabeth Warren and John Curtis have asked Kalshi and Polymarket to explain how they keep insiders out of election markets, giving the companies until Nov. 3, Election Day, to answer seven questions. The bipartisan letter cites candidates who bet on their own races and suspected wash trading on Polymarket’s election contracts.

Key Takeaways

  • Sens. Warren and Curtis sent Kalshi and Polymarket seven questions on election insider trading, due Nov. 3.
  • The senators want each firm’s count of suspected cases since Jan. 1 and how many they referred.

Seven Questions Due on Election Day

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., the ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, and Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, wrote to Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour and Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan in a letter dated Wednesday and released Thursday, asking how the companies stop insider trading and manipulation in election markets. They want written answers by Nov. 3, the day of the midterm elections.

“We are particularly troubled by election-related event contracts,” the senators wrote, noting that the contracts receive prominent coverage and are treated by some observers as indicators of political momentum.

The seven questions ask how each company stops candidates, campaign staff, election officials, pollsters, and others with nonpublic information from trading, how it stops them from getting around trading bans through third parties or affiliated accounts, and how it detects wash trading and other manipulation.

The senators also asked how many suspected cases of insider trading or manipulation in election contracts each company has identified since Jan. 1, how many were stopped before the trades went through rather than found afterward, and how many were referred to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) or law enforcement. They asked whether the companies’ surveillance systems have been independently evaluated, what safeguards will be added before the elections, and how the companies keep election contracts from being confused with polling.

The letter points to cases on Kalshi in which candidates traded on their own races, starting with a 2025 incident the CFTC described in a February advisory. According to the advisory, social media videos in May 2025 appeared to show a candidate trading on a contract tied to his own candidacy, and Kalshi fined the candidate and suspended him for five years. Kalshi disclosed three more such cases in April.

“These examples raise critical questions about how many election-related transactions have escaped detection,” the senators wrote. Separately, they cited NPR reporting on campaign staffers trading on internal polling before its release.

On Polymarket, the letter cites a 2024 Fortune report in which one blockchain analysis firm estimated that roughly one-third of the presidential election market’s trading volume was likely affected by wash trading. It also cites Wired’s finding this month of more than $600 million in trading on Polymarket election contracts involving Ethiopia and Romania. The outlet reported that the Ethiopian market kept trading for months after the vote, and Polymarket had blocked the accounts involved in response.

“The identification of isolated instances of improper trading does not demonstrate that these markets are adequately protected,” the senators wrote, adding that they remain skeptical the companies can police the contracts effectively.

Kalshi Head of Enforcement Robert DeNault told The Hill that “Kalshi prohibits insider trading and market manipulation and proactively blocks candidates and campaign staff from trading to protect market integrity.” A Kalshi source told the outlet that the company uses Federal Election Commission payroll data to block candidates and staffers, and has formed an independent market integrity committee. Polymarket did not immediately respond to The Hill’s request for comment.

Polymarket has investigated dozens of bets tied to the midterms, NPR reported on Oct. 27, with at least two cases referred to the CFTC, according to a person familiar with the investigations. This week, Polymarket is also reviewing dozens of newly created wallets that bet on Benjamin Netanyahu shortly before polls closed in Israel’s election on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.

The letter is dated the same day Curtis’s home state of Utah filed criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders over sports bets. Curtis has backed a bipartisan bill with Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., that would bar CFTC-registered platforms from offering sports contracts, while Warren co-introduced the STOP Corrupt Bets Act in March, part of a broader Democratic push to ban election and sports contracts.

title: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen
summary: Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.
content:
Attackers behind Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion hack still control billions of dollars in stolen cryptocurrency despite efforts by token issuers to freeze the proceeds.

The attack, the largest in crypto history, began at 8:04 pm UTC Thursday and the perpetrators, linked to the same North Korean hackers behind last month’s Bitget hack, immediately began converting assets.

The game plan for the hackers was to convert the assets that could be frozen, like USDT and USDC, into ones that could not, such as Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH).

CertiK engineer Dickson Wu traced $500 million in USDT that was sent to one address, with $325 million sold to market makers for ETH by 20:59 UTC, less than an hour after the hack began.

They were racing against some of crypto’s most powerful gatekeepers: stablecoin giants like Tether and Circle, who had already begun blacklisting addresses associated with the theft.

Binance said Friday that about $3 billion of the stolen assets were frozen onchain out of an estimated $6.3 billion total, and that it is working with law enforcement, issuers and blockchain analytics firms to trace additional funds.

The scale of the theft is mind-boggling, even in crypto terms, but with around half of the assets already frozen, how much of the stolen crypto can the perpetrators actually spend?

Crypto with an off switch

Unlike BTC or ETH, which are decentralized cryptocurrencies with no central issuer and no one to hit the pause button, centralized stablecoins like Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC have issuers that can freeze tokens held at specific addresses.

Binance said it is working with law enforcement to trace the funds. Source: Binance

That gives them the power to act swiftly in incidents like these. Tether froze around $1.567 billion in USDT in total, with the first major freeze happening just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the attacker’s main Ethereum wallet.

Related: Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses

Circle froze around $823 million in USDC three minutes later, with other issuers like Ripple and World Liberty Financial following soon after.

The ability to immobilize crypto is not exclusively a stablecoin feature, and despite not having central issuers, some decentralized protocols like Arbitrum did not sit idly by.

Arbitrum’s Security Council moved around $30.5 million in ARB and ETH into an intermediary frozen wallet, where they can only be moved after further action by the council or a vote by Arbitrum DAO governance.

One important distinction remains — frozen funds don’t necessarily equate to recovered funds. Immobilizing assets prevents the suspected attackers from spending them, but it doesn’t automatically return them to Binance or its users.

The Aave complication

Decentralized lending protocol Aave adds another layer of complexity to the equation. Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, a wallet associated with the attackers deposited $60 million in USDT into Aave V3 on Ethereum and borrowed $44.6 million of wrapped Ether (WETH), around 40 minutes before the first freeze.

LlamaRisk, an Aave risk service provider, said in its 1:00 am update that the attacker’s position subsequently held around $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt. Aave said the position remained overcollateralized and did not put protocol suppliers at risk.

Largest crypto heists of all time. Source: Elliptic

Since the USDT had already been deposited into Aave’s lending pool, blacklisting the attacker’s wallet could not automatically retrieve the collateral held by the protocol, as Aave Chan Initiative founder Marc Zeller explained:

“USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol.”

To prevent further deposits and borrowing, Aave temporarily froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments, although existing users could still withdraw funds, repay loans and liquidate positions.

Aave later lifted its precautionary freeze across V3 and V4 markets, saying its contracts were unaffected and positions remained overcollateralized.

“Just another day in crypto,” Zeller said.

So what can the attackers actually keep?

Elliptic estimated that $2.84 billion had been frozen by 7:00 am UTC on Friday, while the attackers still controlled around $3.33 billion in assets that issuers could not immobilize.

And while the freeze almost halved the attackers’ profit pool, that doesn’t mean all the remaining funds are safe to recover.

Bitcoin and Ether don’t have a centralized token issuer that can blacklist individual addresses like Tether or Circle. So once stolen assets are converted into these native cryptocurrencies, transactions can be restricted, but freezing them is a lot harder.

Binance has pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, and says user assets remain safe; according to the latest update from Binance chief executive Richard Teng, the exchange is already “recovering stolen assets for users.”

title: Weekly Recap: FTMO Founders Discuss Futures Expansion; Plus500 Pushes Guidance Higher
summary:
The retail trading industry saw developments across
proprietary trading, listed derivatives and broker performance this week.
FTMO’s founders discussed the firm’s futures launch, its acquisition of OANDA
and its ambitions to build a larger trading group. Meanwhile, Plus500 raised
its full-year outlo...
content:
The retail trading industry saw developments across proprietary trading, listed derivatives and broker performance this week. FTMO’s founders discussed the firm’s futures launch, its acquisition of OANDA and its ambitions to build a larger trading group. Meanwhile, Plus500 raised its full-year outlook, and NinjaTrader extended its futures platform into the UK.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Quarterly results also highlighted contrasting trends among brokers. CFI reported record trading volumes, while XTB’s profit rose sharply despite lower client trading activity. XTB’s client assets also showed a growing preference for stocks and exchange-traded funds, even as contracts for difference continued to generate most of its trading income.

Elsewhere, institutional trading technology and customer acquisition strategies remained in focus, with analysis examining execution infrastructure and the challenges of reaching forex traders across markets in the Commonwealth of Independent States.

FTMO’s Futures Launch Follows a Decade of Growth and the OANDA Deal

FTMO co-founders Otakar Šuffner and Marek Vašíček discussed the firm’s move into futures trading, its acquisition of OANDA and the challenges facing proprietary trading firms. Founded in 2015, FTMO initially focused on CFDs because it lacked the capital and experience to enter futures.

The company launched its futures offering recently, responding to customer demand and a market where futures evaluations can cost less than comparable CFD and forex challenges. The founders said combining FTMO’s business with OANDA’s established reputation could help distinguish the group from newer firms.

— FTMO.com (@FTMO_com) August 31, 2026

They also discussed regulatory uncertainty, abusive trading groups targeting evaluation systems and the possibility of a future initial public offering.

Plus500 Raises Its 2026 Outlook After Revenue Growth

Plus500 expects full-year 2026 revenue and EBITDA to exceed market expectations, reversing its guidance from July, when it forecast results in line with consensus. Third-quarter revenue rose 11% year on year to $203.2 million, while EBITDA increased 7% to $88.4 million.

Revenue for the first nine months reached $666.1 million, up 11%. New customers rose 27% to 28,747 in the quarter, active customers increased 4% to 119,528 and average revenue per user reached $1,700. Customer deposits hit a quarterly record of $1.9 billion. The company also reported growth in customer trading income, while interest income fell amid lower global interest rates.

NinjaTrader Brings Its Retail Futures Platform to the UK

NinjaTrader has launched its retail futures trading platform in the UK, extending a European rollout that already covers Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands. UK customers can access futures on US equity indices, energy, metals and foreign exchange through CME and Eurex markets.

The platform includes proprietary charting tools, algorithmic trading capabilities and native TradingView integration. NinjaTrader said UK traders had sought direct market access, transparent pricing and execution , and a platform designed specifically for futures.

The launch comes as European brokers explore listed products amid regulatory pressure on CFDs, more experienced retail traders and competition from US firms specialising in futures and options.

CFI Reports Record Quarterly Trading Volume of $3.45 Trillion

CFI Financial Group reported third-quarter notional trading volume of $3.45 trillion, a record for the Dubai-based broker and an increase of about 123% year on year. The figure was 14% higher than in the second quarter. Trading volume for the first nine months reached $8.8 trillion, roughly double the same period last year and already above CFI’s full-year 2025 total of $6.4 trillion.

The company has reported higher volumes in each quarter of 2026, rising from $2.3 trillion in the first quarter to $3.03 trillion in the second. The growth came as the broader broker market tracked by Finance Magnates Intelligence contracted in the second quarter.

XTB’s Quarterly Profit Rises Fourfold Despite Lower Client Trading

XTB reported preliminary third-quarter net profit of PLN 213.7 million, around $54 million, four times the result a year earlier and 6.4% above the average analyst forecast. The figure was nevertheless less than half the PLN 492.2 million recorded in the second quarter. Revenue rose 65.9% year on year to PLN 623.3 million, even as clients traded 18.3% fewer CFD lots.

Revenue per lot nearly doubled to PLN 301 from PLN 152 a year earlier. Commodity CFDs generated 70.8% of the broker’s gross result on financial instruments. The year-on-year comparison reflected a weaker third quarter in 2025, when low market volatility weighed on revenue and profit.

Stocks Dominate XTB Client Assets, While CFDs Drive Trading Income

XTB clients held PLN 56.2 billion, about $14.2 billion, with the broker at the end of September, up by two-thirds since the start of the year. Stocks and exchange-traded funds accounted for 86% of those assets, while open CFD positions represented 1.3%.

However, CFDs continued to generate most of the broker’s trading income, contributing 90.5% of its gross result on financial instruments in the third quarter, based on Finance Magnates’ calculation from XTB’s preliminary report.

That share was down from 96% in the first half. Chief executive Omar Arnaout has said he wants to reduce the contribution from CFDs to around 70%, as investment products attract more clients.

Institutional Traders Put Execution Infrastructure Ahead of Spreads

Trading technology and execution quality are becoming key differentiators for brokers serving institutional clients, according to an analysis of the market. Tight spreads and deep liquidity remain important, but institutions also need pricing aggregation, low latency, smart order routing, automated hedging, reliable market data and systems that can withstand market stress.

They increasingly expect APIs and integration with order management, execution management and transaction cost analysis tools. Paul Golden highlights the difficulty of assessing execution costs for index CFDs, whose prices can be affected by futures markets, dividends and changing conditions.

Brokers may need stronger benchmarks to demonstrate execution quality, while proprietary technology can offer a closer fit for institutional requirements.

Russian-Language Campaigns Missed Audiences in Parts of the CIS

Campaign results across six Commonwealth of Independent States markets suggest that a single Russian-language acquisition strategy may overlook local differences. In an analysis, Stanislav Galandzovskyi found that switching to Uzbek-language creative and adding local payment options Click and Payme reduced the reported cost per acquisition in Uzbekistan from about $650 to around $380.

The markets also differ in purchasing power, regulation and payment access. Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan were described as higher-value opportunities, while Uzbekistan offers scale but lower average deposits. Kyrgyzstan may suit smaller tests.

Tajikistan’s limited disposable income and Turkmenistan’s currency controls, which complicate withdrawals, were cited as barriers. The analysis argued for allocating budgets according to funded-trader acquisition costs before assessing longer-term customer value.

— FTMO.com (@FTMO_com) August 31, 2026

They also discussed regulatory uncertainty, abusive trading groups targeting evaluation systems and the possibility of a future initial public offering.

Plus500 Raises Its 2026 Outlook After Revenue Growth

Plus500 expects full-year 2026 revenue and EBITDA to exceed market expectations, reversing its guidance from July, when it forecast results in line with consensus. Third-quarter revenue rose 11% year on year to $203.2 million, while EBITDA increased 7% to $88.4 million.

Revenue for the first nine months reached $666.1 million, up 11%. New customers rose 27% to 28,747 in the quarter, active customers increased 4% to 119,528 and average revenue per user reached $1,700. Customer deposits hit a quarterly record of $1.9 billion. The company also reported growth in customer trading income, while interest income fell amid lower global interest rates.

NinjaTrader Brings Its Retail Futures Platform to the UK

NinjaTrader has launched its retail futures trading platform in the UK, extending a European rollout that already covers Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands. UK customers can access futures on US equity indices, energy, metals and foreign exchange through CME and Eurex markets.

The platform includes proprietary charting tools, algorithmic trading capabilities and native TradingView integration. NinjaTrader said UK traders had sought direct market access, transparent pricing and execution , and a platform designed specifically for futures.

The launch comes as European brokers explore listed products amid regulatory pressure on CFDs, more experienced retail traders and competition from US firms specialising in futures and options.

CFI Reports Record Quarterly Trading Volume of $3.45 Trillion

CFI Financial Group reported third-quarter notional trading volume of $3.45 trillion, a record for the Dubai-based broker and an increase of about 123% year on year. The figure was 14% higher than in the second quarter. Trading volume for the first nine months reached $8.8 trillion, roughly double the same period last year and already above CFI’s full-year 2025 total of $6.4 trillion.

The company has reported higher volumes in each quarter of 2026, rising from $2.3 trillion in the first quarter to $3.03 trillion in the second. The growth came as the broader broker market tracked by Finance Magnates Intelligence contracted in the second quarter.

XTB’s Quarterly Profit Rises Fourfold Despite Lower Client Trading

XTB reported preliminary third-quarter net profit of PLN 213.7 million, around $54 million, four times the result a year earlier and 6.4% above the average analyst forecast. The figure was nevertheless less than half the PLN 492.2 million recorded in the second quarter. Revenue rose 65.9% year on year to PLN 623.3 million, even as clients traded 18.3% fewer CFD lots.

Revenue per lot nearly doubled to PLN 301 from PLN 152 a year earlier. Commodity CFDs generated 70.8% of the broker’s gross result on financial instruments. The year-on-year comparison reflected a weaker third quarter in 2025, when low market volatility weighed on revenue and profit.

Stocks Dominate XTB Client Assets, While CFDs Drive Trading Income

XTB clients held PLN 56.2 billion, about $14.2 billion, with the broker at the end of September, up by two-thirds since the start of the year. Stocks and exchange-traded funds accounted for 86% of those assets, while open CFD positions represented 1.3%.

However, CFDs continued to generate most of the broker’s trading income, contributing 90.5% of its gross result on financial instruments in the third quarter, based on Finance Magnates’ calculation from XTB’s preliminary report.

That share was down from 96% in the first half. Chief executive Omar Arnaout has said he wants to reduce the contribution from CFDs to around 70%, as investment products attract more clients.

Institutional Traders Put Execution Infrastructure Ahead of Spreads

Trading technology and execution quality are becoming key differentiators for brokers serving institutional clients, according to an analysis of the market. Tight spreads and deep liquidity remain important, but institutions also need pricing aggregation, low latency, smart order routing, automated hedging, reliable market data and systems that can withstand market stress.

They increasingly expect APIs and integration with order management, execution management and transaction cost analysis tools. Paul Golden highlights the difficulty of assessing execution costs for index CFDs, whose prices can be affected by futures markets, dividends and changing conditions.

Brokers may need stronger benchmarks to demonstrate execution quality, while proprietary technology can offer a closer fit for institutional requirements.

Russian-Language Campaigns Missed Audiences in Parts of the CIS

Campaign results across six Commonwealth of Independent States markets suggest that a single Russian-language acquisition strategy may overlook local differences. In an analysis, Stanislav Galandzovskyi found that switching to Uzbek-language creative and adding local payment options Click and Payme reduced the reported cost per acquisition in Uzbekistan from about $650 to around $380.

The markets also differ in purchasing power, regulation and payment access. Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan were described as higher-value opportunities, while Uzbekistan offers scale but lower average deposits. Kyrgyzstan may suit smaller tests.

Tajikistan’s limited disposable income and Turkmenistan’s currency controls, which complicate withdrawals, were cited as barriers. The analysis argued for allocating budgets according to funded-trader acquisition costs before assessing longer-term customer value.

title: A16z, Uniswap Warn Illinois Crypto Tax Rules Could Effectively Ban DeFi
summary: Venture capital giant Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Uniswap Labs, and the DeFi Education Fund are urging Illinois regulators to overhaul proposed cryptocurrency tax regulations, warning that the rules could effectively prohibit decentralized finance (DeFi) activity in the state while exposing users to...
content:
Venture capital giant Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Uniswap Labs, and the DeFi Education Fund are urging Illinois regulators to overhaul proposed cryptocurrency tax regulations, warning that the rules could effectively prohibit decentralized finance (DeFi) activity in the state while exposing users to serious security risks.

Key Takeaways

  • A16z, Uniswap Labs, and the DeFi Education Fund warn that Illinois’ proposed crypto tax rules could effectively ban DeFi by requiring decentralized exchanges to act as tax-collecting brokers, despite their inability to comply.
  • The groups oppose requirements to store customers’ private keys and potentially tax transfers between personal wallets or blockchains. A16z’s Miles Jennings accused regulators of overstepping the law’s authority.
  • Illinois’ 0.2% digital asset transaction tax faces legal challenges from crypto industry groups. Implementation has been delayed until July 2027, and the three organizations are urging regulators to revise the rules and await judicial review.

In a letter submitted Friday, Oct. 30, the three organizations argued that the Illinois Department of Revenue’s proposed implementation of the Digital Asset Tax Act incorrectly treats decentralized exchanges (DEXs) as conventional financial brokers.

The groups contend that DEXs, including the Uniswap protocol, operate through autonomous software rather than intermediaries that control customers’ assets or execute transactions on their behalf. Unlike centralized exchanges, DEXs generally cannot identify customers, determine their locations, collect taxes, or file returns on individual transactions.

The organizations argue that imposing such obligations would make compliance practically impossible, potentially creating a de facto ban on DeFi services in Illinois.

Miles Jennings, head of policy at a16z, criticized the proposal in a post on X Friday, arguing that regulators were expanding the law beyond its intended scope.

“The law is already one of the most anti-innovation bills in the country—a tax on transactions just because they’re digital,” Jennings wrote. He accused Illinois officials of engaging in “politicized rulemaking” that would classify DEXs as tax-collecting brokers, despite their inability to comply.

“Autonomous software is not a person that can collect a tax,” Jennings wrote, adding that the proposal conflicts with federal classifications of decentralized exchanges and Illinois’ own Digital Assets and Consumer Protection Act.

The organizations want regulators to explicitly exclude decentralized protocols and their interfaces from the definition of digital asset brokers, while clarifying that collecting automated protocol fees does not automatically establish broker status.

Private Key Requirement Raises Security Concerns

One particularly controversial provision would require brokers to maintain records containing cryptocurrency private keys, which are used to authorize transactions and control digital assets.

The signatories warn that collecting and storing these sensitive credentials could expose customer funds to theft if the records were compromised. They argue that the requirement conflicts with established cybersecurity practices and could force companies to choose between protecting customer assets and complying with state regulations.

The letter proposes replacing the term “private keys” with “public keys,” which can be used to track blockchain transactions without granting control over customers’ funds. The organizations also object to provisions that could tax withdrawals from centralized exchanges to personal wallets and transfers of assets between blockchains, known as bridging.

Jennings compared the proposed treatment of such transfers to taxing someone simply for moving money between their own bank accounts.

Illinois Tax Already Faces Court Challenges

Illinois enacted its Digital Asset Tax Act in June, imposing a 0.2% tax on the value of qualifying cryptocurrency transactions and other covered digital asset activity. Unlike capital gains taxes, the levy is based on the underlying value of assets involved in covered transactions rather than profits earned.

As previously covered by Bitcoin.com News, the legislation has attracted legal challenges from cryptocurrency industry organizations that argue it discriminates against digital asset activity and creates unreasonable compliance burdens. The Blockchain Association and Crypto Council for Innovation have challenged the law in court, raising concerns about overlapping taxation, constitutional protections, and potential criminal penalties.

Illinois officials subsequently agreed to postpone implementation from January 1 to July 1, 2027, allowing the litigation to proceed. Jennings expressed support for the lawsuits, predicting that the challengers would succeed in overturning the legislation.

“Consumers and entrepreneurs in Illinois deserve better,” he wrote.

The three organizations behind Friday’s letter are asking regulators to delay implementation until at least July 2027 and allow courts to review the tax’s legality before proceeding with the proposed rules.

title: Tether Reports $1.5B Q3 Profit as Total Reserves Reach $191.5B
summary: Stablecoin issuer Tether generated $1.5 billion in net operating profit during the third quarter of 2026, bringing its year-to-date total to $4.5 billion, while reserves backing its tokens reached $191.5 billion, according to its latest financial attestation.   Tether’s Excess Reserves Grow in Q3 Th...
content:
Stablecoin issuer Tether generated $1.5 billion in net operating profit during the third quarter of 2026, bringing its year-to-date total to $4.5 billion, while reserves backing its tokens reached $191.5 billion, according to its latest financial attestation.

Key Takeaways

  • Tether reported $1.5 billion in Q3 net operating profit, bringing its total profit for the first nine months of 2026 to $4.5 billion.
  • Total reserves reached $191.5 billion, against $183.5 billion in liabilities, leaving nearly $8 billion in excess reserves, almost double the previous quarter.
  • U.S. Treasury bills dominated Tether’s reserves, alongside $19.1 billion in precious metals and $8.4 billion in bitcoin, according to an independent attestation by BDO.

Tether’s Excess Reserves Grow in Q3

The company released its third-quarter figures Friday, October 30, showing that total reserve assets stood at $191.45 billion as of September 30, against liabilities of $183.50 billion. The difference left Tether with $7.95 billion in excess reserves, nearly double the $4.1 billion reported at the end of the second quarter.

Tether’s $1.5 billion quarterly net operating profit matched its second-quarter performance, with income primarily generated from its substantial holdings of U.S. Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements. The company reported $4.5 billion in cumulative net operating profit through the first nine months of the year.

The figures were included in an independent attestation prepared by accounting firm BDO, which examined Tether International’s financial position as of September 30.

Tether’s USDT stablecoin supply remained relatively steady at approximately $184 billion through the first three quarters of 2026, despite volatility across cryptocurrency markets. The company said its growing reserve surplus strengthens its ability to honor redemptions during periods of financial stress.

U.S. Treasury bills represented the largest component of Tether’s reserves, totaling $122.84 billion. Including Treasury-backed overnight reverse repurchase agreements, the company’s direct and indirect exposure to U.S. Treasury bills reached approximately $132.4 billion. Overall, cash equivalents and other short-term deposits accounted for $139.58 billion, or approximately 73% of total reserves.

The attestation also detailed $19.08 billion in precious metals, primarily physical gold, alongside $8.37 billion in bitcoin holdings. Other reserve assets included $14.18 billion in secured loans, $6 billion in other investments, and $4.18 billion in publicly traded equities.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the combination of profitability and growing reserves provides financial stability amid geopolitical and market uncertainty.

“Our responsibility is to make sure USDT remains dependable when people need it most, including when markets and financial systems come under pressure,” Ardoino said.

He added that the company’s reserve strategy is intended to preserve liquidity and its ability to meet redemption demands even during difficult market conditions.

BDO concluded that Tether’s September 30 financial figures and reserves report was fairly presented in all material respects under the company’s stated accounting policies. However, the attestation represents a point-in-time assessment rather than a comprehensive audit of the company’s quarterly financial performance.

The report also noted that valuations assume normal market conditions and may not reflect the realizable value of assets during extraordinary disruptions or periods of significant counterparty illiquidity. Despite those qualifications, the results highlight the substantial earnings generated by Tether’s reserve portfolio, even as the supply of its flagship stablecoin remained largely unchanged during the quarter.

On Thursday, Tether played a key role in the response to the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, with Ardoino writing on X that the issuer “froze more than 1.567B USDT” following mass outflows from the leading crypto exchange’s wallets. Freezing the assets means that criminals will be unable to move or exchange the stolen funds, which represent roughly one-quarter of the total USD value of swiped assets.

title: Trezor Warns of Compromised Hardware Wallet Following $93M Ledger Security Scare
summary: Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Trezor has warned customers about a potentially compromised device sold through a former authorized reseller linked to the recent Ledger wallet security scandal, raising concerns that the sophisticated attack may have affected multiple manufacturers. In a Friday ...
content:
Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Trezor has warned customers about a potentially compromised device sold through a former authorized reseller linked to the recent Ledger wallet security scandal, raising concerns that the sophisticated attack may have affected multiple manufacturers.

Key Takeaways

  • Trezor reported a suspected malicious hardware implant in a Safe 5 wallet purchased from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis, potentially exposing users’ recovery phrases.
  • The discovery follows a $93 million Ledger wallet security scandal involving compromised devices distributed through CryptoBilis, prompting Trezor to significantly reduce its reseller network.
  • Trezor urged customers who purchased devices from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to move their funds to new wallets with fresh recovery phrases, while its investigation continues.

In a Friday announcement, Trezor said its security team received a credible report of a malicious hardware implant inside a Trezor Safe 5 purchased from CryptoBilis, a former authorized reseller in Southeast Asia that was also implicated in the Ledger incident.

The affected device was purchased in August through Indonesian e-commerce platform Tokopedia, with the customer reporting the discovery to Trezor on Oct. 28.

According to Trezor, the implant consists of an additional circuit board installed between the wallet’s main board and screen, equipped with a cellular module and antenna. The device allegedly captures information displayed on the screen, including the wallet’s recovery phrase, and transmits it over a mobile network when connected to power.

Trezor said it has reviewed photographs and interviewed the customer but has not yet physically examined the device. The company is treating the report as credible while awaiting laboratory verification.

No funds have been reported stolen from Trezor customers in connection with the suspected compromise, the company said.

Trezor Discovery Follows Ledger Saga

The discovery follows a major security incident involving rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger, which began investigating customer losses on Oct. 9 after reports emerged that devices distributed through CryptoBilis had been physically modified.

Ledger subsequently confirmed that some devices had been compromised in a sophisticated supply chain attack, with reported user cryptocurrency losses estimated at $93 million.

As Bitcoin.com News previously reported, Trezor responded to the Ledger scandal by announcing plans to dramatically reduce its authorized reseller network beginning Jan. 1, 2027, seeking greater control over the distribution of its devices.

At the time, Trezor maintained that it had no evidence of compromised devices bearing its own brand. However, the company had already revoked CryptoBilis’ authorization on Oct. 9 and begun investigating potentially affected products.

Ledger attributed the broader operation to a highly organized criminal group that reportedly spent millions of dollars orchestrating the attack. The manufacturer also said it had inspected samples from its own inventory without identifying compromised units.

Trezor has not established whether the suspected attack on its device was carried out by the same perpetrators responsible for the Ledger compromises.

The company is urging anyone who purchased a Trezor device from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to immediately transfer their cryptocurrency to a new wallet with a newly generated recovery phrase. Simply restoring the potentially compromised wallet’s existing recovery phrase on another device would not eliminate the risk.

Customers who have not yet initialized their devices are being advised against using them. Trezor said affected buyers are eligible for a replacement device shipped directly by the company or a voucher covering the cost of a new wallet.

The company emphasized that its warning applies to all Trezor models purchased through CryptoBilis, although the suspected implant has only been reported in a single Safe 5 device.

Trezor said it has received no similar reports involving other resellers and is coordinating with Ledger and security researchers as the investigation continues.

title: Tether’s excess reserves nearly double to $8B as Q3 profit hits $1.5B
summary: The stablecoin issuer’s US Treasury holdings are comparable to those of major foreign holders, while its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion at the end of September.
content:
Tether reported $1.5 billion in third-quarter operating profit as its excess reserves nearly doubled to $7.95 billion, according to figures released alongside its latest attestation prepared by independent accounting firm BDO.

The company held $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities at the end of September, leaving a reserve surplus of $7.95 billion, nearly double the $4.1 billion reported in June. Its assets included $132.4 billion in direct and indirect US Treasury bill holdings.

That exposure is comparable to South Korea’s $134.2 billion in US government debt and exceeds the United Arab Emirates’ $116.1 billion, according to August data from the US Treasury Department.

Tether also generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first nine months of 2026, with income largely driven by US Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements, according to the company. Its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion, up from approximately $5.8 billion at the end of June.

Tether’s USDT remains the world’s largest stablecoin, accounting for around 60% of the $297.3 billion stablecoin market, according to DefiLlama data. On Friday, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a post on X that USDT’s user base had surpassed 700 million, with adoption concentrated in emerging markets.

The stablecoin issuer has faced years of scrutiny over its reserve transparency. In August, the company announced the completion of its first full independent financial statement audit by KPMG US, although the audited statements were not made public.

title: Coinbase (COIN) Misses Revenue Estimates as Users Fall, Armstrong Sets Up New Share Sales
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase (COIN) Misses Revenue Estimates as Users Fall, Armstrong Sets Up New Share Sales
Coinbase missed revenue expectations as users declined, despite growth in recurring revenue, while executive share-sale plans and a massive Binance security breach added pressure to crypto mar...
content:
Coinbase had a mixed third quarter. Revenue came in at $1.20 billion, below the $1.233 billion analysts expected, according to company filings. Subscription and services revenue did better, reaching $570 million. The company is still heavily tied to trading activity, but its recurring income is growing.

Monthly Transacting Users fell to 7.4 million, down from 9.3 million a year earlier. During its earnings call, Coinbase blamed overall market conditions. Its share of crypto trading volume did rise to 10.7%, the fourth straight quarter of gains, which suggests it is winning business even as the broader market quiets. 

Adjusted EBITDA was $332.9 million, extending a run of 15 straight profitable quarters on that measure. The prediction markets business passed $200 million in annualized revenue, and Coinbase One hit a record number of subscribers.

Coinbase CEO preps share sales

Separately, filings reported on October 30 show CEO Brian Armstrong has set up a plan to sell up to 8.17 million Class A shares. He adopted the plan in August under SEC Rule 10b5-1, which lets executives schedule sales ahead of time. Sales could run from November 16 through October 2027, subject to stock price conditions. Co-founder Fred Ehrsam and President Emilie Choi have similar plans, bringing the total to about 13.6 million shares.

This is not new territory for Armstrong. In the past, VanEck analyst Matthew Sigel tracked about $545.7 million in sales over nine months, starting in April 2025. Armstrong has said these sales are part of his risk management, not a signal about the company.

Coinbase stock slumps nearly 15% 

Coinbase shares (COIN) fell about 15% today, but not necessarily due to this earnings report. 

Binance disclosed a security breach on October 29 that it estimates at $6.3 billion, making it the largest crypto theft on record. Around $3 billion in assets has been frozen so far, with industry partners assisting in the freezes. 

The hackers are allegedly linked to North Korea, though Binance has not attributed the attack to any group. The exchange says it has found no evidence of a leaked wallet private key.

Binance says it has $6.34 billion in reserves available to cover losses. Deposits were unaffected, and the company expects to resume withdrawals within 48 hours. Figures remain preliminary, and estimates vary slightly across outlets.

The market reacted quickly. Bitcoin fell roughly 4.5% to below $77,000. Shares of Strategy (MSTR) fell nearly 10% on the day. Strive (ASST) shares fell over 12% at times. Coinbase’s stock is down over 55% on the year.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance Hack: CZ Fires Back at Elon Musk, Cites $1B SpaceX Stake as Coinbase Offers Security Support
summary: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has urged Elon Musk to stop mocking the exchange after its $6.3 billion security incident, while Coinbase offered assistance.
content:
Skip to content

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has urged Elon Musk to stop mocking the exchange after its $6.3 billion security incident, while Coinbase offered assistance.

The dispute unfolded as Binance worked to contain the October 29 attack, freeze affected assets, and reassure customers that their funds would remain protected. Zhao, widely known as CZ, referred to Binance’s investment in SpaceX while defending the exchange’s financial position. Meanwhile, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said his team was helping block transactions involving compromised wallets and had contacted Binance directly.

Summary

  • Binance founder CZ asked Elon Musk to stop making jokes about the exchange’s $6.3 billion security breach, calling the timing inappropriate.
  • Zhao cited Binance’s SpaceX shares, valued at more than $1 billion, following its $500 million investment in Elon Musk’s Twitter takeover.
  • Binance co-CEO Yi He said the company’s annual revenue was sufficient to cover the losses without selling its SpaceX holdings.
  • Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong offered assistance by blocking transfers to compromised wallets and contacting Binance.
  • Binance reported that approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen and committed to covering all losses through its SAFU fund and company resources.

CZ asks Elon Musk to stop mocking Binance

The disagreement started after Musk reacted to Zhao’s cybersecurity warning and subsequent reports of the attack on Binance.

On October 28, Zhao published a warning on X, advising users against opening suspicious email links or downloading attachments, even when messages appeared to come from trusted contacts. Musk responded with fire and laughing emojis.

CZ urges Elon Musk to stop mocking Binance’s record $6.3 billion hack, citing the crisis’s seriousness while expressing respect for him. Source: X

Following reports of the Binance incident, Musk commented, “Everyday is Zeroday,” referring to zero-day vulnerabilities. These are previously unknown security weaknesses that attackers can exploit before developers have an opportunity to address them.

The exchange continued as details of the security breach emerged. When Zhao’s earlier warning resurfaced, he said he wished more people had followed the advice. He also acknowledged that the attack appeared more complex, adding that compromised devices or algorithms frequently play a role in security incidents.

Musk’s “Everyday is Zeroday” remark underscores the constant threat of zero-day exploits, particularly for high-value crypto platforms. Source: Elon Musk via X

Zhao eventually addressed Musk directly, asking him to stop making jokes while Binance dealt with the financial and operational consequences.

“Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop,” Zhao wrote on X.

He also reminded Musk of Binance’s financial connection to his businesses, pointing to the exchange’s investment in the Twitter acquisition and asking for support during the incident.

Binance’s SpaceX holdings enter the dispute

Zhao’s response brought Binance’s investment in SpaceX into the public discussion. He said the exchange’s stake originated from its $500 million contribution toward Musk’s acquisition of Twitter in 2022.

“Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion,” Zhao wrote.

The statement attracted questions from X users about how an investment in SpaceX related to Binance’s security problems. Zhao subsequently explained that he was referring to the company’s financial resources when assessing its ability to cover the incident’s impact.

His preliminary calculation considered the estimated $6.3 billion impact, approximately $3 billion in frozen assets, and more than $1 billion available through Binance’s Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

Based on those figures, Zhao estimated a potential funding gap of around $2 billion. He described the remaining amount as manageable, although financially painful.

However, the calculation was not a final assessment of Binance’s net losses or the amount of assets that could ultimately be recovered. Zhao also did not announce any plans to sell the company’s SpaceX holdings.

The distinction is important because frozen assets, insurance-style reserves, and company investments represent different sources of financial support. Their availability and eventual use depend on recovery progress and the exchange’s financial decisions.

Yi He says Binance revenue can cover losses

Binance co-CEO Yi He responded to Zhao’s comments, saying the exchange had sufficient annual revenue to absorb the losses without selling its SpaceX investment.

“Reporting to the major shareholder: Our company’s revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares you are bullish on,” she wrote.

Binance’s $500M Twitter takeover investment reportedly grew its SpaceX stake to over $1B amid the security breach dispute. Source: Yi He via X

Zhao subsequently clarified that he had not suggested selling the holdings. Instead, he said he mentioned their value to demonstrate Binance’s available financial resources and potentially reassure Musk about the company’s ability to manage the incident.

The exchange has separately committed to covering all losses using its SAFU reserve and company funds. In an October 30 update, the exchange said it had reserved approximately $6.34 billion in company funds to address the incident.

The exchange also disclosed that it already held around $5 billion in the affected cryptocurrencies and was purchasing the remaining approximately $1.34 billion through market transactions and over-the-counter channels. The objective is to restore affected assets in their original tokens rather than simply compensate users with an equivalent dollar amount.

This reserve is separate from the approximately $3 billion in affected assets frozen with assistance from blockchain partners. The exchange said it would continue working with law enforcement, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms, and other industry participants to trace and recover additional funds.

The exchange also plans to publish updated Proof of Reserves information after the recovery and remediation process is complete.

Binance’s preliminary investigation initially pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and initiate unauthorized withdrawal transactions. The exchange reported no evidence that wallet private keys had been exposed.

Subsequent reporting indicated that investigators were examining additional points of breach. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs estimated that approximately $6.36 billion had moved from Binance wallets across multiple blockchains, with most of the transfers occurring within roughly 20 minutes.

TRM Labs and Chainalysis separately attributed the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor. However, Binance has not publicly confirmed the identity of the attackers and said it was cooperating with law enforcement to establish who was responsible.

Musk’s Binance hack comments draw mixed reactions

Musk’s remarks attracted reactions from cryptocurrency executives, industry participants, and traders as Binance worked to contain the incident.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong offered direct assistance, saying the exchange was helping prevent transfers to wallets associated with the attack. He also confirmed that Coinbase had contacted Binance to offer support.

Brian Armstrong announces Coinbase’s proactive response to the record $6.3B Binance hack. Source: Brian Armstrong via X

“Our team is doing everything we can to support in the current situation, including blocking sends to compromised wallets,” Armstrong wrote.

He added, “Moments like this call for the industry to work together.”

The response highlighted the role of cooperation between cryptocurrency exchanges and blockchain service providers during security incidents. Tether and Circle also helped freeze assets linked to the attack, contributing to the comapny’s reported recovery efforts.

Meanwhile, the breach placed additional pressure on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin and other digital assets faced selling pressure following the incident, with Bitcoin briefly approaching six-week lows near $76,000 as concerns about exchange security affected market sentiment.

Coinbase reaffirmed its security measures, monitored Binance’s crisis, and offered support, including blocking transfers to compromised wallets. Source: Coinbase via X

Binance’s operational restrictions also became an important concern for customers. The exchange initially suspended deposits and withdrawals while reviewing its security systems and affected withdrawal addresses. In a subsequent service update, the exchange confirmed that deposits were operating normally, while withdrawals remained paused during a security revamp. It expected withdrawal services to resume within 48 hours of the October 30 update.

The exchange reiterated that user funds would remain protected and pledged to publish a detailed technical report once its investigation was complete.

The public disagreement between Zhao and Musk has added another dimension to Binance’s recovery efforts. While Zhao has pointed to the exchange’s financial resources and SpaceX investment, Yi He has said annual revenue can cover the shortfall without selling those holdings. Coinbase’s offer of assistance has also demonstrated how competing exchanges can coordinate when a security incident affects the wider cryptocurrency industry.

Crypto Briefing reported that the Secret Service confirmed its cooperation with Circle on October 30, a day after the breach. Reuters separately reported, citing a person familiar with the matter, that Binance is working with both the FBI and the Secret Service.

FBI Coordinates Binance Hack Investigation

The FBI said it was aware of the incident and was working with public- and private-sector partners to assess its impact and coordinate investigative steps.

Circle has frozen more than $800 million in USDC linked to the breach, according to its CEO, Jeremy Allaire, who said the action was taken in coordination with law enforcement. Tether has also frozen nearly $1.57 billion in related USDT, according to CEO Paolo Ardoino.

JUST IN: 🇺🇸 US Secret Service is working with Circle to identify, freeze, and recover funds stolen from Binance. https://t.co/v8kGqYRh5r

— Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru) October 30, 2026

The freezes by the two stablecoin issuers total more than $2.37 billion. Binance has put the total value of assets frozen by industry partners at around $3 billion, including actions by other firms.

Circle and Tether can freeze their stablecoins at specific blockchain addresses, allowing them to restrict transfers linked to the incident. However, frozen assets have not necessarily been recovered or returned to affected users.

TRM, A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea’s elite hacking unit. “We make this judgment with high confidence,” the firm said in a post on its website Thursday. https://t.co/jQtTVPVJGQ

— NBC 6 South Florida (@nbc6) October 30, 2026

TRM Attributes Binance Attack to “North Korea”

Separately, blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group, with “high confidence”. TRM said its assessment was based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The firm is tracking the funds and alerting industry partners through its Beacon Network.

CFTC Cites Binance Hack in Registration Push

Separately, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig cited the Binance breach as support for a proposed voluntary registration framework for offshore cryptocurrency exchanges serving US retail traders. Under the plan, participating platforms would be required to meet US cybersecurity and customer protection standards. Selig said broader federal registration would require congressional action. The CFTC is targeting December 14, 2026, for the proposed rulemaking.

title: New Breach Points: Binance CEO Reveals Fresh Findings in $6.3B Hack
summary: Binance investigators uncovered additional breach points, bypassed approval controls, and evidence-destruction tactics in Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack, co-CEO Richard Teng said. His update outlined a withdrawal-service rebuild, a companywide security review, and targets for restoring transfers and v...
content:
Binance investigators uncovered additional breach points, bypassed approval controls, and evidence-destruction tactics in Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack, co-CEO Richard Teng said. His update outlined a withdrawal-service rebuild, a companywide security review, and targets for restoring transfers and verifying reserves.

Key Takeaways

  • CEO Richard Teng said the attacker bypassed Binance’s normal approval controls.
  • A self-destruct mechanism destroyed attack tools and traces, he said.
  • Teng hoped withdrawals could resume within 40 hours, subject to testing.

Investigation Expands Beyond the Laptop

Binance found additional breach points beyond the initially suspected engineer laptop while investigating the $6.3 billion hack, co-CEO Richard Teng said.

In a video shared on Oct. 30, he stated: “This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.”

Teng described evidence destruction:

“This was a complex attack. The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate.”

His earlier statement explaining the attack process emphasized: “To be clear: The attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”

Signing Controls Come Under Scrutiny

Explaining the approval failure, Teng stated: “The attacker used a known multi-signature protocol EIP-7702, to obtain on-chain execution approval over a hot wallet. That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls.” The executive continued:

“That’s why we need to pause the withdrawal service to investigate, rebuild, and retest the entire infrastructure system.”

Ethereum’s EIP-7702 feature lets a wallet authorize smart contract code to act on its behalf, including moving assets. Delegating malicious code can give an attacker control over those holdings, while multisignature approval is a separate control requiring multiple signatures.

Independent TRM Labs analysis of Binance’s signing systems pointed to a compromise of its signing infrastructure across blockchains. The firm cited valid signatures from wallets using different keys and signing schemes as evidence that attackers could make Binance’s systems authorize transfers. That finding concerned control over the transaction-signing process, while Teng had reported no evidence of a private key leak.

Separately, Elliptic’s onchain assessment of the breach identified 50 pre-signed authorizations on Ethereum. One enabled delegation to attacker-controlled code, which repeatedly drained the affected wallet as new funds arrived.

Company Funds Back the Coverage Pledge

Corporate funding reserved to cover losses exceeded $6.34 billion, Teng said. Of that, $5 billion was already held in affected tokens, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH, and BNB. Remaining token purchases were proceeding through market and over-the-counter channels to replace assets affected by the hack.

In the video, the Binance CEO committed company funds to covering all losses, while earlier statements also identified the Secure Asset Fund for Users, or SAFU. Teng had reassured customers:

“Bottom line—your money is safe, and we’re covering every loss.”

He credited retained crypto earnings with enabling coverage and described long-term reinvestment in the business and security.

On assets held under exchange custody, he stated: “We NEVER use any customer funds, so they are not impacted. What was affected in this incident was Binance’s own hot wallet. User assets are held under Binance’s established security architecture. The vast majority sit in cold wallets, and are only moved into a hot wallet when a user makes a withdrawal.”

Withdrawal Restart Awaits Testing

Teng outlined the conditions for restoring withdrawals: “We are rebuilding the withdrawal service, and we are not switching it back on until it passes rigorous testing.” He further shared:

“We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to our Sunday deadline, which is on track to be within 40 hours.”

The companywide security review was examining endpoints, cloud infrastructure, key management, and signing systems as part of the response.

Earlier updates reported normal deposits, revoked affected address authorizations, and approximately $3 billion in frozen assets from partners. Law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers, and other exchanges were pursuing recovery and accountability. Teng thanked users for their patience and partners for their rapid assistance, saying Binance worked nonstop to make users whole.

Alongside plans for a technical postmortem after investigators verified the findings, Teng advised concerned users to check their balances and contact support. Teng pledged a full proof-of-reserves report by Monday, Nov. 2, with an initial view potentially available earlier.

title: Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3B Binance hack
summary: Circle, Strategy and other crypto-linked stocks fell sharply Friday, a day after Binance disclosed a $6.3 billion security breach.
content:
Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.

Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.

Source: Yahoo Finance

The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN (IREN), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR), which dropped about 9%.

The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of a the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

Related: Binance working with FBI to recover assets following $6.3B hack

Crypto gains lift Coinbase, Strategy profits as revenue falls

Coinbase and Strategy both reported third-quarter earnings Thursday, with gains on their crypto holdings lifting profits even as revenue declined.

Coinbase reported $719 million in net income, boosted by about $715 million in gains on cryptocurrency investments. Adjusted net income, which excludes investment gains and other items, was $78 million. Net revenue fell about 34% year over year to $1.16 billion.

The exchange also reported that its prediction markets business surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue.

Strategy reported $19.53 billion in net income, largely driven by a $20.91 billion gain in the value of its Bitcoin (BTC) holdings. Revenue declined 3% year over year to $125.4 million.

Strategy also announced that Andrew Kang will step down as chief financial officer on Nov. 5.
