title: Google AI Spending Shock: Alphabet Loses Over $500 Billion After Q3 Earnings Miss
summary: Alphabet shares plunged nearly 13% on October 29 after the Google parent reported third-quarter results below Wall Street forecasts, wiping roughly half a trillion dollars from its market value.
content:
Skip to content

Alphabet shares plunged nearly 13% on October 29 after the Google parent reported third-quarter results below Wall Street forecasts, wiping roughly half a trillion dollars from its market value.

The sell-off followed disappointing advertising revenue, slower Google Search growth, and rising concerns over the cost of its AI expansion. Despite strong Google Cloud performance, investors questioned whether Alphabet’s growing infrastructure investments could generate sufficient returns.

Alphabet Q3 Revenue Miss Raises Google Search Concerns

Alphabet reported third-quarter revenue of $127.6 billion, representing a 25% increase from $102.3 billion a year earlier. However, the result missed analysts’ expectations of approximately $128.2 billion, according to LSEG data.

Sundar Pichai reported Alphabet’s Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% year-over-year to $127.6 billion, driven by AI-led growth across its businesses. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

Google advertising revenue reached $82.01 billion, falling about $1.4 billion short of market estimates. Within that segment, Google Search and other advertising revenue increased 12% to $63.35 billion, compared with 17% growth in the previous quarter. YouTube advertising revenue also increased 9% to $11.2 billion.

The slowdown has drawn attention to Google’s expanding use of AI-powered search features. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler indicated that increased adoption of AI Mode contributed to the deceleration in search advertising growth. The conversational interface encourages longer interactions, but those queries currently generate less advertising revenue per use than traditional search.

Foreign-exchange movements also affected the quarterly comparison. However, investors remain concerned about how Google’s transition toward AI-generated search experiences could affect its established advertising model.

The issue was highlighted by Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. He said, “In a market worried about AI cannibalizing the franchise, investors need to see search accelerating, not decelerating.”

His comments reflect a central concern surrounding Alphabet’s AI strategy: maintaining search engagement while ensuring that new AI experiences continue to generate advertising revenue.

AI Infrastructure Spending Drives Negative Free Cash Flow

Alphabet’s increasing AI investment was another source of investor concern. The company recorded $51.4 billion in capital expenditure during the third quarter, with most of the spending directed toward technical infrastructure supporting AI development and cloud services.

Alphabet reported its first negative free cash flow in 22 years, reaching $9.07 billion as aggressive AI infrastructure investments drove heavy spending on data centers and cloud capacity. Source: Reuters via X

The investment contributed to negative free cash flow of approximately $9.07 billion, compared with a $5.9 billion deficit in the previous quarter. It marked the second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow and a significant change for a company that had historically generated substantial cash from its operations.

Alphabet’s management said the deficit reflected the cost of expanding technical infrastructure, alongside inventory accumulation for Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems and a $5.2 billion cash payment related to a European Commission fine.

The spending also coincided with a decline in reported earnings. Alphabet’s net income available to common shareholders fell 25% year over year to $26.17 billion. Diluted earnings per share came in at $2.12, while the company’s adjusted EPS was reported at $2.67, below the $3.02 analyst estimate.

An unrealized investment loss also affected the results. Alphabet reported negative $8.2 billion in other income and expenses, primarily because of a decline in the value of its SpaceX investment. The non-cash accounting loss reduced reported earnings but was separate from the company’s infrastructure expenditure.

Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi maintained Alphabet’s 2026 capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion. However, she told analysts that spending would increase significantly in 2027, without providing a specific figure.

This outlook has raised questions about how quickly the company’s AI investments can translate into additional earnings and sustainable cash generation.

Google Cloud Growth and Gemini AI Demand Offer Support

Despite the pressure on advertising, Google Cloud delivered one of Alphabet’s strongest quarterly performances. Revenue increased 103% year over year to $30.71 billion, supported by demand for AI infrastructure, enterprise services, and computing capacity.

Alphabet ($GOOGL) fell nearly 13% after missing Q3 2026 revenue and EPS estimates, as slowing search ad growth and investment losses weighed on investor sentiment. Source: @KobeissiLetter via X

Cloud operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, while its operating margin expanded to 36.2%, compared with 23.7% in the same quarter last year. Alphabet also reported a $561 billion cloud backlog, reflecting substantial contracted demand for its services.

The company’s AI products showed further growth. Alphabet’s first-party model APIs were processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, representing a 40% increase from the previous quarter. The Gemini app also reached one billion users, while the company introduced additional models through its Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon lineup.

CEO Sundar Pichai pointed to increased search engagement as evidence that the company’s AI investments were supporting product usage. He said the year-over-year Search query growth rate was “the highest it’s been in the last five years.”

These developments offer a different perspective from the market’s reaction. Google Cloud is benefiting from enterprise demand, while Gemini adoption and AI-powered search are expanding the company’s reach.

However, the immediate challenge remains monetization. Alphabet must demonstrate that increased AI usage can generate enough advertising and subscription revenue to justify the substantial costs of building and operating its infrastructure.

GOOG Technical Analysis: $280 Support in Focus

Alphabet’s Class C shares (NASDAQ: GOOG) closed at approximately $282.32 on October 29, down 12.29% during the session. The stock also traded near $278.29 at its intraday low, reflecting strong selling pressure following the earnings announcement.

Alphabet Inc (Google) Class C price chart. Source: TradingView

The decline pushed shares below several important short- and medium-term moving averages. TradingView’s technical indicators point to a bearish short-term structure, with downward-sloping averages reinforcing the recent selling pressure. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has also moved toward oversold territory.

However, an oversold RSI reading does not independently confirm a bullish reversal. Traders may look for stabilization and a confirmed recovery above nearby resistance before treating the decline as a potential trend change.

On the downside, the $275-$280 region represents an immediate support area. A sustained break below this zone could expose the stock to additional historical demand levels.

On the upside, the $290 level represents initial resistance, followed by the psychological $300 mark. A broader resistance region extends toward $328.50, where previously broken support levels could influence future price movements.

A sustained recovery above $300 would provide an early indication that selling pressure is easing. Until then, the technical structure remains under pressure, with buyers needing to defend the lower support region.

AI Investment Returns Remain Alphabet’s Biggest Test

Alphabet’s latest earnings highlight the growing gap between AI demand and the financial cost of meeting it. Google Cloud, Gemini, and AI infrastructure services are attracting customers, but the company is also committing increasingly large sums to data centers, servers, networking equipment, and custom processors.

The pressure could continue into 2027. Management has already indicated that capital expenditure will rise significantly, while greater use of third-party computing capacity could weigh on cloud margins in the near term.

For investors, the central question is whether AI can strengthen Google’s existing businesses without weakening the economics of traditional search advertising. Alphabet’s expanding cloud business offers an important source of growth, but its search operations remain critical to overall revenue generation.

The latest sell-off shows that investors are increasingly focused on the financial returns from AI rather than spending commitments and product launches alone. Alphabet’s ability to convert growing AI adoption into higher revenue, improved margins, and positive free cash flow could become an important factor in determining the stock’s next direction.

title: Crypto Biz: Bitcoin’s quantum threat is becoming an economic problem
summary: Bitcoin faces mounting quantum security concerns as Ripple secures a US banking charter, USDC gains ground in Europe and VanEck adds BTC to a new ETF.
content:
The debate over quantum computing has raised serious questions about Bitcoin’s long-term security, but the economic consequences could emerge long before the technology seriously threatens the network.

Muneeb Ali, founder of Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, believes quantum computing risks are already discouraging institutional investment, even as US spot Bitcoin ETFs have amassed more than $104 billion in net assets, according to BitBo data. He warns that BTC has only a few years to prepare for the transition to quantum-resistant security, a process that could take years given the network’s history of slow and contentious upgrades.

For institutional investors drawn to Bitcoin as a hedge against currency debasement, doubts about its long-term security could complicate the investment case. 

This week’s Crypto Biz explores the quantum threat, alongside new developments surrounding Ripple, VanEck and European stablecoin adoption. 

Quantum computing fears are already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says

Bitcoin could face a more serious security challenge if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum resistance by 2028, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network’s lengthy upgrade process leaves little room for delays.

Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Ali said Bitcoin needs a credible roadmap for becoming quantum-resistant, with meaningful progress required by 2028. He cited 2030 as the target for completing the transition to quantum-resistant security, based on guidance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, though advances in artificial intelligence could bring that deadline forward.

Even if developers agree on how to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks, implementing the changes could take years. Holders would then need time to move their Bitcoin to quantum-resistant addresses.

Although some industry participants dispute the urgency of the threat, Ali argued that uncertainty alone could undermine investor confidence. He also warned that a quantum breakthrough capable of compromising Bitcoin would have consequences for the broader cryptocurrency market.

Ripple secures US federal banking charter

Ripple has received final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, clearing the last regulatory hurdle after securing conditional approval in December 2025.

The newly chartered Ripple National Trust Bank will operate under federal supervision, manage reserves backing the company’s RLUSD stablecoin, serve as a collateral trustee for tokenholders and provide digital asset custody. RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, which is regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse welcomed the approval, declaring that “crypto and banks work better together.”

The decision follows similar final approval for Circle in July, while Coinbase, Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge remain at the conditional approval stage. Unlike traditional commercial banks, national trust banks generally cannot accept deposits or issue loans and do not carry Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation coverage.

USDC overtakes Tether in euro trading as MiCA rules take hold

Circle’s USDC has surpassed Tether’s USDt in stablecoin trading against the euro, as European Union regulations reshape competition between the world’s two largest dollar-backed stablecoins.

According to a new report from Kaiko, USDC now accounts for 56% of euro-denominated stablecoin trading, up from just 10% in January 2024. The shift accelerated after major cryptocurrency exchanges restricted USDt trading for European Economic Area customers to comply with the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

USDC’s euro order books are now roughly 40% deeper than USDt’s, suggesting stronger liquidity for traders. However, USDT remains the dominant stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply approximately 2.5 times larger than USDC’s.

The findings come after the European Banking Authority designated USDC as the bloc’s first “significant e-money token,” subjecting it to additional regulatory oversight. Kaiko suggested that the US GENIUS Act could produce similar changes in stablecoin trading, depending on how exchanges implement the new requirements.

VanEck includes Bitcoin in new multi-asset ETF

VanEck, the $244 billion asset manager, has launched an actively managed exchange-traded fund that combines traditional stocks and bonds with real assets and a small allocation to Bitcoin.

The VanEck Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO), announced Tuesday, invests in a mix of VanEck and third-party ETFs and targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, which can range from 1% to 5%. Rather than holding Bitcoin directly, the fund gains exposure through a spot Bitcoin exchange-traded product. The launch expands VanEck’s existing Wealth Builder model portfolios into a single ETF. 

David Schassler, VanEck’s head of multi-asset solutions, said the traditional 60/40 stock-and-bond portfolio was designed for a different investment environment. He contended that adding real assets could help investors navigate a broader range of economic conditions, with Bitcoin now forming a small part of that strategy.

Crypto Biz is your weekly pulse on the business behind blockchain and crypto, delivered directly to your inbox every Thursday.

title: Bitcoin Price Rebounds Above $77K, but Binance Hack Keeps Traders on Edge
summary: Bitcoin stabilized above $77,000 after a $6.3 billion Binance hack triggered a marketwide sell-off, pushing the cryptocurrency to a multiweek low of $76,320. Bitcoin Plunges to Multiweek Low Following Binance Hack Bitcoin price stabilized above $77,000 following a marketwide sell-off triggered by Th...
content:
Bitcoin stabilized above $77,000 after a $6.3 billion Binance hack triggered a marketwide sell-off, pushing the cryptocurrency to a multiweek low of $76,320.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin fell to $76,320 after Binance disclosed a $6.3 billion hack, triggering widespread panic.
  • Bitcoin’s plunge fueled $1.66 billion in crypto liquidations, with long positions suffering most.
  • Global Settlement Network’s CEO urged stronger custody safeguards after the $6.3 billion breach.

Bitcoin Plunges to Multiweek Low Following Binance Hack

Bitcoin price stabilized above $77,000 following a marketwide sell-off triggered by Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack of Binance, which briefly dragged the cryptocurrency down toward $76,000, its lowest level since Aug. 21. The downturn came shortly after bitcoin approached $82,000 earlier Thursday on the back of strong U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) data.

According to Bitstamp data, bitcoin initially shed more than $2,500 shortly after news of the hack broke Thursday afternoon, finding temporary support above $78,200. A brief recovery quickly gave way to relentless selling pressure, as investors shaken by the size of the attack drove the token down to $76,320.

Bitcoin rallied from $76,400 to nearly $79,000 between midnight and 10 a.m. EST before again dropping below $76,500. A second attempt to regain ground failed short of the $78,000 mark. By 1:00 p.m. EST, the leading cryptocurrency by market cap was trading at $77,255, reflecting a daily decline of 4.7%.

Friday’s losses left bitcoin on the cusp of ending October down more than 7%, while widening the cryptocurrency’s year-to-date losses to more than 11%. The losses also dragged bitcoin’s market capitalization to $1.55 trillion, which in turn helped drag the broader crypto economy’s market cap to approximately $2.7 trillion.

Crypto Liquidations Hit $1.66 Billion

As Binance revealed hackers had stolen $6.3 billion in digital assets, ongoing price volatility drove bitcoin liquidations above $500 million. As of this writing, the tally sits at $556 million over the past 24 hours, per Coinglass.

Long positions bore the brunt of the damage, accounting for 83%, or roughly $464 million, of the wiped-out bets, while short liquidations totaled nearly $92 million. Across the broader crypto market, liquidations hit $1.66 billion, led by $1.45 billion in long position wipeouts.

Meanwhile, analysts warn that the breach of a major cryptocurrency exchange underscores the industry’s wider security vulnerabilities. While AI tools are increasingly helping attackers, recurring breaches across nearly every major exchange suggest security measures remain far from foolproof.

Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and CEO of Global Settlement Network, argued that Binance’s reliance on external assistance to mitigate the attack points to deeper systemic issues.

“We’re talking about the world’s largest crypto exchange relying on emergency freezes and reimbursement promises to contain a multibillion-dollar incident,” Kirkley said. “That’s a serious problem for an industry asking institutions to trust it with substantially more capital. For me, the takeaway is simple. Institutions need more than assurances that their money is safe. They need verifiable ownership, proper controls, and reliable access to their assets, particularly when markets are under pressure.”

Consequently, while crypto leaders pour resources into lobbying Washington for regulatory favors, Kirkley warned that the industry’s most existential threats aren’t coming from lawmakers; they are coming from rapid advances in cybercrime and AI.

“The CLARITY Act and the election outcome will matter for regulatory certainty, but institutions need a financial system they can rely on regardless of who’s in Washington,” he added. “Political influence can help shape legislation. It can’t compensate for weak custody, unreliable access, or poor operational controls.”

title: Recap: How Binance’s record $6.3B hack unfolded
summary: A recap of Cointelegraph’s live coverage of the Binance hack, including early breach reports and the exchange’s full reimbursement pledge.
content:
This recap summarizes Cointelegraph’s reporting on the Binance hack and has been updated with the exchange’s latest statements. The investigation is ongoing, and figures and recovery timelines may change. See our archived live coverage for the original timeline.

Hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance on Thursday, in what is now the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. Industry partners have frozen roughly $3 billion in affected assets, while customers await the reopening of withdrawals.

TRM Labs traced the first unauthorized transfers to around 8:05 pm UTC Thursday, with Binance wallets drained across multiple blockchains. The attackers targeted hot wallets, which exchanges keep connected to the internet to process withdrawals.

TRM attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025. Binance has not publicly confirmed the attackers’ identity.

“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” said Binance co-CEO Richard Teng. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”

Binance said it had reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the affected tokens. However, that allocation excludes the frozen assets, and the exchange said it was buying the remaining tokens through exchanges and over-the-counter deals.

A spokesperson told Cointelegraph the $5 billion was in Binance’s custody but declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security concerns. Security firm CertiK said it needed more information to verify the holdings independently.

Frozen funds are not necessarily recovered funds, and Binance has yet to disclose how much stolen crypto has actually been returned to its control.

EIP-7702’s role in the hack comes under scrutiny 

Ethereum’s EIP-7702 upgrade came under fire after attackers used it to drain a Binance wallet. EIP-7702 is a feature that lets a wallet authorize software to act on its behalf. Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph that compromised signing systems likely enabled the theft.

Attackers could have stolen the funds without EIP-7702, but it may have helped them bypass safeguards and drain assets in one sweep, Ben-Natan said.

Teng said that the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to gain execution authority over a hot wallet without passing Binance’s normal approval controls. A “self-destruct mechanism” destroyed tools and traces, complicating the investigation, he said.

Binance said investigators had also uncovered additional breaches beyond the initially suspected compromised laptop. However, it reported no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked and said it expected to share further technical findings within about 48 hours.

Chainalysis observed thousands of transactions in quick succession that could indicate automated laundering, with funds circulating among addresses and sometimes returning to wallets used earlier.

Binance users await withdrawals reopening

The theft rattled crypto prices and prompted a precautionary freeze on new deposits and borrowing at decentralized lender Aave. Aave reopened its markets Friday afternoon, while Binance’s withdrawals remained suspended.

Binance said in a Friday update that it aimed to begin reopening withdrawals in stages Sunday, Nov. 1, subject to completing security checks. Deposits and other unaffected services remained operational.

The exchange said it planned to take an initial proof-of-reserves snapshot within 12 hours of the announcement, with results ready by Monday. The report is intended to show the assets Binance holds and the backing of customer balances.

Magazine: Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express

title: As it happened: Binance’s record $6.3B crypto hack
summary: How Binance’s $6.3 billion hack unfolded, from the first onchain alerts to $3 billion in frozen funds and a widening security investigation.
content:
Live coverage has ended. The updates below document Cointelegraph’s reporting on the record $6.3 billion Binance hack as events unfolded.

What we know about the Binance hack:

  • Binance says the estimated total impact is around $6.3 billion and the verified total value of crypto frozen is $3 billion. This could increase as investigators trace additional assets.
  • Binance says deposits are operating normally, and withdrawals are expected to resume as scheduled.
  • Assets frozen include Tether USDt (USDT), USDC (USDC), Ripple USD (RLUSD), World Liberty Financial USD (USD1), StraitsX USD (XUSD), USDT0 (USDT0), Wrapped Beacon ETH (WBETH), Tether Gold (XAUT), Pax Gold (PAXG), Pax Dollar (USDP) and Arbitrum (ARB).
  • Cybersecurity analysts suspect North Korea’s TraderTraitor is behind the attack.
  • Binance says investigators have uncovered additional points of breach after initially pointing to a potentially compromised engineer’s laptop.
  • Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the same tokens stolen.

Oct. 30 at 2:34 pm UTC

Binance targets withdrawals within 40 hours, reserves report by Monday

Binance is aiming to resume withdrawals within 40 hours and publish a full proof-of-reserves report by Monday, co-CEO Richard Teng said.

Teng said the exchange hopes to restore access before its Sunday deadline and provide an initial reserves snapshot ahead of Monday’s report.

Teng also disclosed that the attacker used a “self-destruct mechanism” to destroy tools and traces during the breach, complicating the investigation.

The attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to gain execution authority over a hot wallet, Teng said. That delegation “did not pass through our normal approval controls.”

Oct. 30 at 1:57 pm UTC

Aave lifts precautionary freeze across all V3 and V4 markets

New deposits and borrowing have resumed across all Aave V3 and V4 markets after a precautionary freeze following the Binance hack, the lending protocol said.

Withdrawals and repayments remained available throughout the freeze. Aave said its contracts were unaffected by the incident.

Founder Stani Kulechov confirmed that lending and borrowing were re-enabled, saying all positions remained overcollateralized.

Oct. 30 at 1:11 pm UTC

Binance working with FBI to recover assets following $6.3B hack

Binance is working with the FBI to help recover some of the funds stolen in the record $6.3 billion exploit, according to a source familiar with the matter said.

The cryptocurrency exchange revealed its cooperation with law enforcement in an X post, without specifying the agencies involved.

Oct. 30 at 12:41 pm UTC

Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses

A Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the $5 billion in matching tokens is held in the exchange’s custody.

The spokesperson declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security reasons. Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.

The exchange also said it submits weekly reports on company funds to Abu Dhabi’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority under a requirement that predated the hack.

Oct. 30 at 11:07 am UTC

Yi He says Binance is buying altcoins to replace stolen tokens

Binance is buying altcoins in quantities matching those stolen in the hack as it prepares updated proof of reserves, co-CEO Yi He said.

The purchases are being made through over-the-counter deals and on exchanges, she said.

Binance’s SAFU fund and company holdings include substantial amounts of Bitcoin and Ether, Yi He said. The exchange would provide another update once the purchases were complete.

Oct. 30 at 11:00 am UTC

EIP-7702 may have helped Binance hackers bypass security checks

Attackers could have stolen Binance’s funds without Ethereum’s EIP-7702 upgrade, but it may have helped them bypass security checks, Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph.

Ben-Natan said compromised signing systems likely enabled the attack. EIP-7702 provided “a way to do this in one sweep,” while attackers otherwise would have needed multiple transactions.

Ambire CEO Ivo Georgiev also said the funds could have been stolen through other methods. He warned that exchange engineers could overlook the need to revoke malicious EIP-7702 delegations after regaining control of their systems.

Oct. 30 at 10:55 am UTC

Binance says it reserved $6.34B in company funds for hack losses

Binance has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the hack, the exchange said.

The company said $5 billion of those funds were already held in the same tokens affected by the attack. It was purchasing the remaining assets through market and over-the-counter transactions to address token shortfalls.

Some purchases could take longer because of low liquidity and OTC settlement times, Binance said.

The allocation excludes frozen or protected assets. About $3 billion remained frozen, with efforts to recover those funds continuing alongside law enforcement and industry partners.

Oct. 30 at 10:09 am UTC

Binance hackers may be automating laundering, Chainalysis says

The attackers behind Binance’s hack may be using automation to move and redistribute stolen funds, blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said.

“Our investigators are observing never-seen-before laundering patterns with the stolen funds from the Binance exploit,” the company said.

“Thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation to obscure the trail of funds.”

Chainalysis said funds repeatedly circulated among addresses, sometimes returning to wallets used earlier in the sequence.

Oct. 30 at 08:37 am UTC

Binance finds additional breach points in hack investigation

Binance’s investigation into its $6.3 billion hack has uncovered “additional points of breach,” the exchange said, after initially pointing to a potentially compromised laptop.

The exchange said it was still gathering facts in coordination with law enforcement.

Binance said it remained on track to resume withdrawals in 45 hours, while deposits remained unaffected. Outflows from the exchange stopped when it paused withdrawals, it said.

Oct. 30 at 07:37 am UTC

Teng says Binance hack was not a single “one-click” action

The attacker behind Binance’s $6.3 billion hack did not simply use one engineer’s permissions to carry out the breach, co-CEO Richard Teng said.

In an X post, Teng said the incident involved “a more complex attack process” and was not a single “one-click” action.

“Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual,” he wrote.

Teng reiterated that preliminary findings pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which may have allowed the attacker to access an internal service and submit unauthorized withdrawals. He said investigators had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak.

Binance would cover all losses using its SAFU fund and company funds, he said.

Oct. 30 at 05:01 am UTC

Analysts suspect North Korean group behind Binance hack

Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin said the Binance hack was likely carried out by North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor, citing links to a previous hack.

In a post on X, Levin put the theft at $6.4 billion, slightly above Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion impact. He said industry partners had frozen approximately $3 billion and Chainalysis was continuing to track the funds.

In a separate post, onchain investigator ZachXBT said the stolen funds from the Binance attack and the earlier Bitget exploit were commingled in the same address on Friday, after arriving via THORChain.

“This indicates the same actor is likely behind both incidents,” he said.

“The Bitget exploit was attributed to DPRK-linked TraiderTraitor, which had overlap with other previous exploits such as Kelp DAO,” he added.

Speaking to Cointelegraph, Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan also said the attack resembled the work of North Korea, or DPRK, based on the sophisticated onchain preparations, customer sweeper contract and multiple authorizations.

TRM Labs has also attributed the attack to TraderTraitor with “high confidence,” which it said is “based on robust on and off-chain intelligence.”

TraderTraitor has also been named by the FBI as the same group responsible for the ByBit hack in February last year.

Oct. 30 at 4:17 am UTC

Binance expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours

Binance said withdrawals remain paused while it completes a security revamp of its withdrawal service and related addresses, with service expected to resume within 48 hours. Deposits are operating normally.

The exchange said the incident involved multiple factors and that its security team was tracing the full attack path through a compromised computer, which they suspect to be the entry point.

Oct. 30 at 03:49 am UTC

Binance hack could accelerate shift to DEXs: Standard Chartered

The Binance hack could push more crypto trading toward decentralized exchanges and benefit Uniswap over the longer term, according to Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, Geoffrey Kendrick.

In an email shared with Cointelegraph, Kendrick retained his $100 price target for Uniswap’s UNI token by 2030, saying the breach was “another reason why that forecast may end up being too low.”

CoinGecko research shows that the top 10 spot DEX-to-CEX ratio was 23.5% in the second quarter of 2026, climbing 2.1 percentage points from the first quarter of 2026. 

“I would encourage investors to re-engage with Uniswap,” said Kendrick. “The decentralized exchange (DEX) has never had any exploits, and the hack of the largest centralized exchange (CEX), in Binance, should see the ratio of DEX to CEX trading continue to increase.” 

Oct. 30 at 02:25 am UTC

Binance points to engineer’s hacked laptop in $6.3B breach

Binance said its initial investigation into the multi-billion crypto breach has pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. 

The exchange said the laptop compromise may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. It said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak, though its investigation remains ongoing.

The crypto exchange has also disclosed that the estimated total impact of the hack is $6.3 billion. 

Oct. 30 at 02:21 am UTC

First Digital confirms it has frozen FDUSD involved in attack

First Digital CEO Vincent Chok said it has frozen the FDUSD stolen in the attack on Binance. 

“We’re working alongside the Binance team and will share updates as we have them,” Chok told Cointelegraph in a written statement. 

“Our priority is protecting FDUSD holders and stopping bad actors from moving stolen funds. Protecting users is a responsibility we all share.”

Oct. 30 at 01:19 am UTC

Bitcoin trades below $77,000 as BNB falls 8% 

Bitcoin traded near $76,937, down 4.9% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. BNB fell 8% to about $693, while Ether declined 5.7% to about $2,211.

DeFi tokens also fell, with AAVE down 11.3% and Uniswap’s UNI down 10.7% over the same period.

The Bitcoin Fear and Greed Index, which tracks Bitcoin market sentiment, fell to “fear” with a score of 30, which it has not seen since August.

Oct. 30 at 12:52 am UTC

Binance says $3 billion frozen from hack

Binance said the current verified amount of assets frozen from the hack is now $3 billion.

The update came after the Arbitrum Security Council said it executed a transaction to freeze $30.5 million from the Binance exploit, involving 74.6 million Arbitrum (ARB) and 8,425 Ether (ETH).

“The Security Council acted by weighing its commitment to the security and integrity of the Arbitrum community and Arbitrum governance without impacting any Arbitrum users or applications,” it said.

“As of October 30, 2026 time, the funds have been successfully transferred to an intermediary frozen wallet,” it said.

The funds will no longer be accessible to the address that originally held the funds and can only be moved by further action of the Security Council or a vote of Arbitrum DAO governance, it added.

Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC

Chainalysis estimates $5.9 billion stolen from Binance

Chainalysis said its current estimate of the amount stolen from Binance is $5.912 billion at the time of theft, four times the amount stolen from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.

Binance earlier said the verified total frozen is $2.54 billion.

Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC

Blockaid suspects Binance hack involved private key “misuse”

The suspected multi-billion-dollar Binance hack may have involved attackers manipulating the exchange’s transaction-signing signature, according to Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan.

Speaking to Cointelegraph, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key. 

“It seems to be… a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.

Ben-Natan said this was a preliminary assessment, drawing on their experience with similar attacks and their observations of the onchain activity.

Arkham CEO Miguel Morel said the attack appears to be ongoing.

Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC

Binance says deposits temporarily suspended

Binance said it has temporarily suspended deposits as it conducts security checks, freezes funds and coordinates with law enforcement. It previously confirmed it had suspended withdrawals.

“We are working around the clock and will share a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete,” the company said, adding it will “cover all losses.”

Earlier, Binance also said it had temporarily suspended Binance Alpha trading.

Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC

Wintermute and GSR disclose Binance exposure

Crypto trading firms Wintermute and GSR disclosed exposure to Binance but said they did not expect major disruption to their businesses.

The firms are market makers, which place buy and sell orders on exchanges to help other traders complete transactions. A disruption to their operations could make trading harder or more expensive across crypto markets.

GSR CEO Xin Song said its Binance exposure was less than 5% of its net equity, meaning the value of its assets minus its liabilities. He said GSR was working with Binance to understand the incident and identify ways to help.

Wintermute CEO Evgeny Gaevoy said his firm’s exposure was less than 20% of net equity and that he did not expect operational disruption.

Neither executive disclosed a dollar amount for the exposure or confirmed financial losses.

Oct. 29 at 11:40 pm UTC

Ripple freezes RLUSD linked to Binance hack

Ripple is freezing holdings of its dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin linked to the Binance hack, according to Jack McDonald, the company’s senior vice president of stablecoins.

McDonald said Ripple was “actively freezing affected funds” and coordinating with relevant parties to support the investigation. He did not disclose the amount frozen.

Oct. 29 at 11:35 pm UTC

Binance says $2.54 billion frozen after hack

Binance said the verified total of assets frozen in connection with the hack had reached $2.54 billion, clarifying differing figures circulating publicly, including references to $1.8 billion.

The exchange said the total could increase as its teams work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets. Binance said it would publish further figures once verified.

Oct. 29 at 10:36 pm UTC

World Liberty Financial freezes $27 million in USD1 

World Liberty Financial has frozen $27 million in US-dollar-pegged stablecoin USD1 and $2 million worth of WLFI, according to Binance co-founder Yi He. 

“USD1 has taken proactive steps to freeze the $27 million in USD1 associated with the Binance hack,” said World Liberty Financial co-founder and CEO Zach Witkoff. 

World Liberty Financial said it worked with BitGo to freeze the stolen WLFI and USD1 funds. 

“We will cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation and support efforts to hold those responsible accountable. Protecting our users remains a top priority,” said World Liberty in a post on X. 

Oct. 29 at 10:33 pm UTC

Binance says withdrawals will resume once issues resolved

Binance says its team is conducting security checks and will resume withdrawals as soon as the “security issue” is resolved.

Oct. 29 at 10:32 pm UTC

Aave freezes markets after Binance exploiter borrows $44.6 million

Decentralized lending protocol Aave froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments as a precaution following the Binance hack.

In a governance forum update posted after the freeze, risk service provider LlamaRisk said the Binance exploiter deposited 60 million USDT and borrowed 19,762 Wrapped Ether (WETH), worth about $44.6 million at the time.

The borrowing occurred between 8:58 pm and 9:01 pm UTC on Oct. 29, about 40 minutes before the first freeze. It was the exploiter’s only Aave position across all networks and versions, with no further interactions detected after 9:01 pm UTC.

The position remained backed by $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt at the update’s snapshot. LlamaRisk said it remained subject to normal liquidation and did not put Aave suppliers at risk.

The freezes covered 175 reserves on V3 across 16 networks and 117 reserves on V4 across four networks.

Users can still withdraw funds and repay loans, and liquidations continue. However, the freeze prevents new deposits and borrowing, including additional collateral deposits, leaving repayment as the only way to improve an existing position’s health factor.

LlamaRisk said markets would remain frozen until the exploiter’s funds stopped moving and Binance provided greater clarity on containment, followed by a staged reopening. It warned that a prolonged freeze could push borrowing rates higher as withdrawals reduce available liquidity.

Oct. 29 at 9:15 pm UTC

Binance investigates multibillion-dollar security breach

Binance is investigating a potential multibillion-dollar security breach involving one of its Ethereum wallets, after suspicious transfers prompted stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle to reportedly freeze billions in assets.

A Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph on Thursday that the exchange was investigating reports of a potential security issue but had not confirmed any impact on user funds. The spokesperson said its security teams were reviewing the activity and would provide updates once more information was verified.

Concerns were first raised by blockchain researcher Spreek, who posted on X that assets from a Binance-linked Ethereum wallet had been transferred to a newly created address through a contract call allegedly funded by Tornado Cash. Spreek later reported that wallets connected to the transfers had begun selling Tether USDt (USDT) through decentralized exchanges.

Blockchain analytics platform Arkham Intelligence later identified a collection of wallets labeled “binance-hacker-1029” holding approximately $5.84 billion in digital assets. The figure represents the wallets’ reported holdings rather than a confirmed estimate of stolen funds.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the activity appeared to be a hack, adding that Tether and Circle had frozen approximately $971 million and $823 million, respectively. Zhao said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.

Tether, Circle freeze over $2.36 billion

Blockchain security firm Blockaid said its team had identified roughly $3.3 billion in suspicious transfers involving Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Avalanche.

Shortly after news of the hack emerged, Tether and Circle, the two largest stablecoin issuers by market capitalization, said they had frozen a combined $2.36 billion in tokens linked to the suspected incident.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement and would continue supporting the investigation.

A few minutes later, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.567 billion in USDT linked to the potential exploit.

“Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority,” Ardoino wrote.

The Binance hack came hours after Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a compromise at a third-party provider. The prediction market platform said it had fixed the issue and pledged to reimburse affected users, with all systems reported operational by 7:05 p.m. UTC Thursday.

Reporting by Felix Ng, Bryan O’Shea, Nate Kostar and Yohan Yun.

title: Bitcoin risks worst October in 12 years as tech sell-off spreads to gold
summary: Bitcoin circled $77,000 as crypto markets navigated US stock-market downside, while the gold price fell to its lowest in a year.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) stayed under pressure below $80,000 at Friday’s Wall Street open as AI fears returned to intensify a broader risk-asset rout.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin struggled to hold around $77,000 as risk assets fell across the board at the US open.
  • The Nasdaq Composite Index fell to 25,500, its lowest levels since early August, while gold dropped to $3,891 per ounce for the first time since October 2025.
  • BTC/USD risked sealing October losses or 7.7%, the most since 2014.

Tech contagion ramps up as Nasdaq drops 2.5%

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD down 1.1% on the day after dropping to its lowest levels since Sept. 18.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

US stock markets opened sharply lower as traders reacted to weak forward guidance from tech giants. Intel, which on Thursday warned of weaker Q4 sales than markets had anticipated, saw its stock price drop by nearly 30% on Friday’s open.

The sell-off weighed on both tech giants and chipmakers, with analysis warning of fresh challenges to AI-sector confidence. 

“With renewed fears over AI Monetization, the Equity rotation is likely to continue today but the broader indices will reflect Tech’s downside,” JPMorgan wrote in a note, quoted by CNBC.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was 2.5% lower at the time of writing at around 25,500, a level last seen on Aug. 3.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Beyond stocks, contagion spread to precious metals, with gold trading as low as $3,891 per ounce, its weakest in a year. 

XAU/USD one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Bitcoin on track for weakest October since 2014

Crypto markets continued to deal with the aftermath of a multi-billion dollar hack of Binance, the largest crypto exchange. 

Related: Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?

The platform said that it would cover the losses with its own capital after the theft of $6.3 billion in coins and tokens. A spokesperson told Cointelegraph that Binance had $5 billion in matching tokens currently available.

Commenting on the outlook for crypto, trading company QCP Capital warned that macro conditions, tech-sector fears and the Binance hack had “created a period of heightened market repricing.”

“Technology sector earnings guidance regarding future capital expenditure will remain a critical variable for understanding the trajectory of artificial intelligence infrastructure investment and expected profitability,” it summarized in analysis on Friday.

At $77,000, BTC/USD was set to close the month 7.7% lower — its worst October performance since 2014, per data from CoinGlass.

BTC/USD monthly returns. Source: CoinGlass

title: How Bitcoin Is Helping Reshape Online Slots
summary:
Bitcoin (BTC) is changing different aspects of handling money. Yet, online gaming platforms are one area you might not have come across. By looking at how the introduction of this
The post How Bitcoin Is Helping Reshape Online Slots appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) is changing different aspects of handling money. Yet, online gaming platforms are one area you might not have come across. By looking at how the introduction of this cryptocurrency and other digital assets has changed the scene, you can understand another way in which Bitcoin is causing a positive impact.

  • Instant Access to Games and Fast Withdrawals
  • Flexible Gaming Options With No Fiat Currency Worries

Instant Access to Games and Fast Withdrawals

The length of time taken for a transfer is one of the major issues with fiat currencies and traditional banking methods. In terms of online slot games, players have generally had to wait several days for withdrawals to reach their bank account or for a physical check to arrive.

When sending crypto funds to a gaming platform, deposits arrive almost instantly and withdrawals are processed rapidly by reputable gaming operators. By using the blockchain, the platform ensures that transfers go through very fast, without any need for banks or other middlemen to approve them. Other cryptos, such as Litecoin (LTC), Tron (TRX), and Cardano (ADA), are also commonly accepted, which gives players more choice and flexibility.

A Growing Player Base Reflected in More Themes and Features

The diverse range of games in this Bitcoin gaming platform confirms that this is a growing market. The slots section includes freshly released titles, covering themes as far-ranging as mythology, wild animals, and sports. They also have a variety of features, such as jackpots, bonus rounds, and free spins. The fact that players can sign up and fund their accounts so quickly has allowed this industry to reach out to a new audience, which is reflected in the games being released. Some of the games even use crypto imagery to make them stand out.

Classic slots featuring symbols like fruits and bells can also be played. The crypto aspect simply means that players can get started more quickly and receive any winnings without any delay. As BTC continues its move toward mainstream acceptance, there will be more people playing games in this way, which will lead to greater levels of demand for new slot themes and features.

Flexible Gaming Options With No Fiat Currency Worries

Using fiat currencies for online gaming was the only possible approach in the past, but it never fully suited the online approach to slots for many players. It could be argued that cryptos fit more naturally into the way that online slots have evolved, as they can be used for flexible gaming transactions.

This is particularly true for anyone who wants to avoid uncertainty with their local fiat currency. It’s no coincidence that Bitcoin and other digital assets have gained ground more rapidly in countries where the national currency has lacked stability and where inflation has been a major problem.

By using cryptos to access online slots, users avoid the risk of sticking to a currency that could rapidly lose value due to inflation. Bitcoin is known for its volatility, but it’s also worth taking into account that its entire mining process is based on the idea of the token being worth more over time, since it becomes increasingly difficult to mine through the halving process.

If you prefer a digital asset that retains the same value day after day, a stablecoin like Tether (USDT) is an option that gives you exactly that. Stablecoins are pegged to the value of a real-world asset. In the case of USDT, this is the US Dollar. So, one Tether is always worth $1. This removes a lot of the potential price fluctuations that might make online gaming transactions more volatile than you would like.

A More Private, Secure Approach

Finally, for many people, it’s the privacy and security of digital assets that make them a sound choice. These tokens allow you to send money anywhere in the world on a pseudonymous basis. The reason that most cryptos aren’t fully anonymous is that someone could theoretically track your transactions until they find one that reveals your identity, which is typically at the fiat on-ramp or off-ramp stage.

Despite this, a lot of people feel more comfortable using cryptos for their online gaming funds. It’s definitely more private than sending from your bank account or normal debit card. In this way, you add a layer of extra security to your online activity as well. The transparency of the blockchain and the high level of password security mean that it’s far more difficult for anyone to illegally access your funds. Privacy-focused tokens like Litecoin offer an even higher degree of privacy.

Since you need to send your funds from a self-custody wallet to your gaming account, it’s important that you choose the right type of wallet and then store the password details securely. Thankfully, there are now more user-friendly crypto wallet options than ever before.

The option of using crypto to access online slot games has made it easier for more people to play in this way, without having to learn all the details of blockchain technology.

title: SEC Charges Two Companies in $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Charges Two Companies in $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme
The SEC has charged two companies with defrauding investors of over $130 million through a crypto Ponzi-like scheme.
This post SEC Charges Two Companies in $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme first appeared on Bitcoin M...
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission charged two foreign-operated, Colorado-incorporated companies with running a crypto investment fraud that used false federal filings to raise more than $130 million from tens of thousands of retail investors.

The defendants are BG Wealth Sharing Ltd. and DSJ Exchange Pty Ltd. A complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California alleges that from at least October 2025 through June 2026, the companies induced investors in more than 40 states and several U.S. territories to join a “wealth-sharing program.” 

Participants were promised risk-free returns generated by so-called signals for crypto asset trading.

According to the complaint, BG Wealth claimed to be the world’s largest hedge fund, claimed registration with the SEC as an investment adviser, and said it partnered with a licensed and secure crypto trading platform, DSJ Exchange. 

The SEC says none of those claims were true. The complaint alleges the companies submitted false Form ADV and Form D filings to the SEC. Those filings were viewable on the agency’s website and shared with investors as evidence that the SEC had licensed or approved the firms.

Laura D’Allaird, chief of the SEC Enforcement Division’s Cyber and Emerging Technologies Unit, described the operation in a statement. 

SEC: Crypto scheme was ‘a Ponzi-like tactic’

“This alleged scheme was well-planned,” she said, citing social media, encrypted messaging channels, weekly live videoconferences and a mobile app used to engage investors. The complaint alleges the defendants displayed fake certificates bearing the SEC’s seal and made periodic payments to some investors, “a Ponzi-like tactic,” while misappropriating the remaining funds.

The SEC charged both companies with violating the antifraud provisions of the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

It charged BG Wealth with violating Sections 204(a) and 207 of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The agency seeks permanent injunctions, disgorgement with prejudgment interest, and civil penalties against both companies, along with conduct-based injunctions against BG Wealth.

The Form ADV and Form D filings have been removed from the SEC website.

The SEC’s Office of Investor Education and Assistance has issued investor alerts warning that scammers are using exempt reporting adviser filings to create a false impression of legitimacy. The agency encourages investors to check the background of anyone offering or selling a crypto investment through Investor.gov.

The SEC said it received assistance from the Alberta Securities Commission, the Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, the Texas State Securities Board, the Utah Division of Securities, the Washington State Department of Financial Institutions, the Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions, and other authorities.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Chainalysis and TRM Labs have linked yesterday’s $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.
This post Blockchain Firms Link North Korea to $6.3 Billion Binance Hack  first appeared on Bitcoin Magaz...
content:
Blockchain analysis firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs have linked the $6.3 billion Binance hack yesterday to TraderTraitor, a unit associated with North Korea. If confirmed at this scale, the theft would be the largest crypto hack on record. 

Chainalysis puts the total at $6.4 billion in its own assessment. Chainalysis says funds began leaving Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains around 4:20 p.m. Eastern Time on October 29. 

The firm said the attacker used an operational wallet funded through Tornado Cash to submit signed authorizations that allowed a Binance hot wallet to run attacker-deployed code. 

The attacker then swept assets into addresses under its control. Binance has said its initial investigation points to a compromised engineer’s laptop, which gave an attacker access to a service container and enabled unauthorized withdrawals. 

The exchange said it has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak.

The attacker reportedly tried to outpace freezes by converting stablecoins into ether and other assets that issuers cannot freeze. Chainalysis said the attacker swapped $325 million in stablecoins into $285 million in ETH over roughly 20 minutes, then sent the remaining $175 million to stopover wallets. Freezes began by 5:14 p.m. Eastern, according to the firm.

Market reacts to the hack

Bitcoin dropped toward $76,000 on Friday morning before trading near $77,400. Other crypto followed suit and posted declines of their own. Total market liquidations reached $1.5 billion, with bitcoin accounting for $468 million and ether for $358 million. 

Long positions, which bet on higher prices, bore most of the losses. The sell-off coincided with a separate incident at decentralized betting platform Polymarket, which suspended international trading after hackers drained more than $2.6 million from user accounts.

Binance said Thursday that the security incident affected about $6.3 billion in assets, surpassing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of 2025, which was attributed to North Korean hackers. Former CEO Changpeng Zhao wrote on X, “It does look like a hack.” Zhao no longer runs the exchange but remains a key shareholder.

Stablecoin issuers moved to contain the fallout. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze more than $1.567 billion in USDT and that protecting the industry and its partners is its main priority. 

Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said Circle froze more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. First Digital CEO Vincent Chok said FDUSD stolen in the attack has been frozen. Binance says about $3 billion has been frozen onchain in total.

Binance has enough funds to cover the incident

Binance says it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the incident. About $5 billion of that reserve is held in the same token assets that were affected, and the company is buying the remainder through market and OTC channels. 

The exchange says frozen and protected assets remain subject to verification and plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves. 

Reuters, citing a person familiar with the matter, reported that Binance is working with the FBI and the U.S. Secret Service.

Bitcoin may have further downside

Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, Geoffrey Kendrick, wrote in an email to CoinDesk that the negative price action may have some way to go. He said a new base will form after assets are unfrozen and more details of the hack emerge. 

Kendrick argued that the incident could accelerate a shift toward decentralized exchanges. Chainalysis has warned that scammers are impersonating the firm, including those offering fund recovery and recruiting services. 

Victims should treat unsolicited recovery offers with caution and rely on official channels for updates.

At the time of writing, Bitcoin is trading near $76,700.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Coinbase led a selloff in crypto-linked stocks following Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack. Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses from the attack, which cybersecurity analysts have linked to a North Korean hacking group.

Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3B Binance hack

Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.

Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.

The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN (IREN), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR), which dropped about 9%.

The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses

Binance said Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from its hack, with $5 billion already in held in the same tokens stolen.

“The $5 billion is held in the exact token assets that are required. These assets are in Binance custody,” a Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.

The spokesperson declined to disclose the wallet addresses, citing security reasons, but said that the holdings would appear in the exchange’s next proof-of-reserves report, which shows the assets it holds to back customer balances.

Binance said it provides weekly reports on its company funds to the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi Global Market in the United Arab Emirates. The exchange said the requirement predated the hack.

Binance hit by $6.3 billion hack, analysts suspect North Korean group

Crypto exchange Binance said it has been hit with a security breach with an estimated $6.3 billion impact, with its initial investigation pointing to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that may have allowed attackers to submit unauthorized withdrawals.

The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak.

Industry partners helped freeze approximately $3 billion in affected assets. Binance pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, saying user funds were safe.

Cybersecurity analysts have pointed to North Korean group TraderTraitor as likely having carried out the attack, citing links to a previous hack.

Withdrawals remain paused during a security revamp, with Binance expecting to resume within 48 hours.

title: How to Buy Bitcoin in 2026: 5 Platforms Compared for Beginners
summary:
Your first Bitcoin purchase should feel simple. A few early choices make that easier. Start by deciding how much effort you want to spend and what you plan to do
The post How to Buy Bitcoin in 2026: 5 Platforms Compared for Beginners  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Your first Bitcoin purchase should feel simple. A few early choices make that easier. Start by deciding how much effort you want to spend and what you plan to do with the coins. Many beginners feel pressure to buy a large amount at once. A small first order lets you learn the process with little at stake.

  •       Ease of use. Look for a clear sign-up flow and a plain checkout screen. Beginner-friendly platforms show the price, the fee and the amount of Bitcoin you receive before you confirm. Customer support matters if something goes wrong.
  •       Payment options. Pick a platform that supports a payment method you already use. Bank transfers usually cost less. Cards and digital wallets are faster. A platform with several options gives you a fallback if one method fails.
  •       Fees. Costs come in several forms. A platform may charge a percentage fee, a spread built into the price, or both. Network fees apply when you withdraw to your own wallet. Beginners often focus on the headline fee and miss the spread. Always read the final quote.
  •       Speed. Instant payment methods usually deliver Bitcoin to your account within minutes. Bank transfers can take days. Moving coins to your own wallet depends on the Bitcoin network, where a first confirmation arrives in about 10 minutes on average. This overview of how Bitcoin mining works explains why.

Two more points deserve attention. Decide whether you want to keep Bitcoin on the platform or send it to a wallet you control. A guide to Bitcoin economics and network security covers the background. Then confirm that the service is available in your country and check what identity verification it asks for.

Here are five ways to get started.

  • 1. Paybis
  • 2. Cash App
  • 3. Strike
  • 4. River
  • 5. Bitpanda
  • Bitcoin Buying Platforms Compared: Fees, Payments, and Availability
  • Conclusion

1. Paybis

Paybis offers several ways to pay. Cards and PayPal are accepted, and bank transfers are available too. The platform serves customers in 180+ countries and lists 90+ cryptocurrencies. Beginners who already use PayPal can buy Bitcoin with PayPal, and the Paybis homepage covers the other options.

2. Cash App

Cash App offers Bitcoin purchases inside its money app. The minimum purchase is $1. Fees are tiered by order size. Cash App lists 2.0% for orders from $1 to $499 and 0% for orders of $2,000 or more. A spread of up to 0.75% may also apply to market buys, and it appears on the confirmation screen.

Auto Invest, which buys on a schedule, carries no fee. Standard withdrawals complete in 24 hours or less. The Bitcoin page refers to US states and territories. It also says Bitcoin services are not licensable in all of them, so check eligibility first.

3. Strike

Strike is an app that focuses on Bitcoin. You can fund purchases with a linked bank account or a wire transfer. Debit card purchases are available too. A single buy can range from $1 to $2.5 million.

Strike says its fees are as low as 0.49% and fall as your volume grows. You can schedule recurring buys to spread your purchases over time. For personal accounts, Strike waives recurring-buy fees after the first week. App availability and some features depend on your jurisdiction.

4. River

River is a platform that focuses on Bitcoin. Its fee page lists 1.00% on one-time orders up to $1 million. Direct deposit and recurring buys are listed at 0%. For recurring buys, the waiver starts seven days after the first order, and that first order carries the standard fee.

The minimum fee is $0.01, and a price spread may also apply. The fee page does not say which payment methods or countries are supported. Check both on the River website before you sign up.

5. Bitpanda

Bitpanda describes itself as an Austria-based broker regulated in Europe. Its Bitcoin page lists a long set of payment options. These include bank transfers and cards. PayPal and Klarna are listed too.

The page does not publish a fee figure or a minimum purchase, so read the quote before you confirm. It also does not list supported countries. Check eligibility before you create an account.

Bitcoin Buying Platforms Compared: Fees, Payments, and Availability

RiverCheck on the website1.00% on one-time orders, 0% on recurring buys after week oneBitcoin focus
BitpandaBank transfers, cards, PayPal and moreNot stated on the Bitcoin pageEurope-based broker

Fees and availability change often. Treat the table as a starting point and read each platform’s current terms.

Read the payment options column first. It shows whether you can start with a method you already trust. Then compare fees at your usual order size, because tiered fees change with the amount. A $50 purchase and a $5,000 purchase can carry very different percentages on the same platform. Last, check availability. A platform that does not serve your country is off the list.

Conclusion

The easiest option depends on how you want to pay and how often you plan to buy. Some platforms suit a single purchase. Others reward regular buying with lower fees.

Recurring buys deserve a look. They spread your purchases over time. That removes the pressure of picking one perfect entry price.

Start small for your first order. Read the final quote before you confirm. Check how long the payment takes to clear. Then decide whether to leave your Bitcoin on the platform or send it to your own wallet. If you choose a wallet, double-check the address before you send anything.

Keep a record of each purchase. Dates, amounts and fees help when you report taxes later. Tax rules differ by country, so check local guidance.

Finally, confirm that the platform operates in your country. Read its verification requirements before you deposit funds.

content:
U.S. pressure to hold Treasuries forces central banks to sell what they can, says Doomberg, setting up a wildly bullish long-term case for gold and Bitcoin.

What happens to reserve assets when you’re not allowed to sell them? Doomberg argues that U.S. pressure on allies to hold their Treasuries changes the math for central banks, and that in a crisis “you sell what you can sell, not what you want to sell.” That explains gold’s short-term weakness since February 28th, but in the long run he sees it as wildly bullish for gold and Bitcoin as neutral reserve assets. He also shares why younger, hyper-online generations are more likely to choose Bitcoin.

Friday, 30/10/2026 | 12:00 GMT by Sylwester Majewski

  • Recent consolidation in gold and major CFDs has compressed broker revenues, but early 2026 spikes in VIX above 30 suggest sharp volatility swings may soon return.
  • With the 3 November US midterms approaching, retail desks could see an influx of returning traders as election-driven uncertainty historically lifts transaction frequency.

Financial markets have experienced a period of relatively smaller activity in recent weeks, with several major instruments trading within narrow ranges. Gold, which has emerged as one of the main drivers of retail CFD trading volumes in recent years, has also experienced a period of consolidation.

For brokers, such conditions can translate into lower trading activity, fewer transactions and reduced revenue opportunities. The question is whether the current stagnation reflects a temporary pause before another period of increased market volatility. One potential catalyst is approaching. On 3 November 2026, the United States will hold its midterm elections, determining the composition of Congress for the remaining two years of President Donald Trump's term.

London's trading industry is coming home!

arket Volatility and Its Implications for Retail Trading Activity

Volatility is an important reason for trading activity in financial markets. Larger and more frequent price movements can create additional opportunities for speculative trading, encouraging existing investors to increase transaction frequency and attracting previously inactive traders back to the market. For retail brokers, whose revenues depend partly on trading activity, changes in market volatility can therefore have a real effect on business performance.

The relationship between expected and actual market volatility provides additional context. Finance Magnates Intelligence's comparison of VIX with one-month realised S&P 500 volatility shows that the two measures frequently move in the same direction, although the magnitude and timing of their movements differ. During February and March 2026, VIX rose above 30, while realised volatility increased subsequently, reaching approximately 20–22%. A similar relationship is visible in oil markets, where the Cboe Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index (OVX) climbed above 120 in February, preceding a substantial increase in realised oil volatility towards 80–90% during March.

These observations illustrate how elevated implied volatility can precede periods of stronger actual price fluctuations. They do not, by themselves, establish a corresponding increase in retail trading volumes, but they help explain why forward-looking volatility indicators may be relevant to brokers anticipating changes in market activity.

Correlation Between VIX and Retail CFD Trading Volumes

Is there any relationship between market volatility and retail CFD volumes? As our next chart shows, although retail volumes have followed a steady upward trend since January 2022, periods of increased VIX readings often coincide with higher retail CFD volumes. This suggests that market uncertainty attracts greater attention from retail investors, particularly when volatility rises sharply.

content:

We picked these eight with three tests: forex leverage of at least 1:500, at least one Tier-1 or Tier-2 license at group level, and no accounts for US residents. Six brokers pass all three, IUX misses the license test, and MultiBank’s terms do not mention US clients. The highest leverage comes from offshore entities, while the same brands’ UK, EU, and Australian companies follow a 1:30 cap and stricter client rules.

In this article, we will compare the eight brokers, explain margin calls and stop-outs, and show how far a price can move before your account closes, then cover safety and country limits. The eight brokers compare on leverage and protection as follows:

What are the Best High Leverage Forex Brokers in 2026?

The best high leverage forex brokers on this list each win on a different point, so here is each broker’s top forex leverage with the strength that sets it apart:

  • XM (1:1000): XM is a long-running multi-license brand.
  • PrimeXBT (1:1000 to 1:2000): PrimeXBT pairs forex CFDs with crypto futures.
  • IUX (1:3000): IUX offers very high leverage from a $30 deposit.
  • IC Markets (1:5000): IC Markets has the highest forex leverage on this list.
  • MultiBank (1:1000): MultiBank has the widest license coverage.
  • BlackBull (1:500): BlackBull offers the widest platform choice.
  • FP Markets (1:500): FP Markets offers low-cost Raw account pricing.
  • Eightcap (1:500): Eightcap offers the deepest TradingView integration.

1. XM

XM is a forex and CFD broker whose EU company, Trading Point of Financial Instruments Ltd, has held a CySEC license since 2010, while its global site runs under Belize’s FSC. The company reports more than 20 million clients in over 190 countries, which gives XM the largest reported client base here.

Pros and Cons of XM

The pros and cons of XM come down to a low entry point and stable margin rules on one side, and offshore regulation for its 1:1000 accounts on the other.

  • Low deposit: Standard and Ultra Low accounts open with $5.
  • Stable margin: XM says its margin does not change overnight or at weekends.
  • Negative balance protection: XM states that all accounts carry it.
  • Offshore entity: The 1:1000 leverage comes from XM Global Limited in Belize.
  • Low stop-out: At 20%, losses grow larger before positions close.
  • Limited access: XM does not serve the US, Canada, Israel, or Iran.

XM Leverage by Entity and Account Protections

XM gives 1:1000 through XM Global Limited under the FSC of Belize, while its EU company follows the 1:30 retail cap, and both promise negative balance protection.

International clients join XM Global Limited, which keeps negative balance protection but not the EU’s 50% close-out rule. XM does not accept US residents.

2. PrimeXBT

PrimeXBT is a multi-asset broker active since 2018, and its regulations page lists a South African company under the FSCA and an El Salvador company with crypto licenses. Traders who want currencies and crypto in one place are the reason PrimeXBT is here, because its PXTrader platform carries forex CFDs and crypto futures side by side.

Pros and Cons of PrimeXBT

The pros and cons of PrimeXBT come down to cheap entry and stated protection on one side, and unclear leverage and entity details on the other.

  • Low entry: PrimeXBT says an MT5 Pro account opens with $1.
  • Two markets: PXTrader lists forex CFDs next to crypto futures.
  • Negative balance protection: PrimeXBT states your balance never drops below zero.
  • Unclear leverage: Its pages list MT5 Pro at both 2000x and 1:1000.
  • Entity not named: PrimeXBT does not say which company offers MT5.
  • Slow top-up: Covering a negative balance can take up to an hour.

PrimeXBT Leverage by Entity and Account Protections

PrimeXBT names no entity behind its highest leverage, and its negative balance protection is the only account protection it states for any of the three companies on its regulations page.
